title: Creating a sub-task in the modernized create dialog fails with "Security level is required" when the user is not a member of the scheme's default security level
description: h3. Issue Summary In company-managed spaces where the Security Level field is required and present on the sub-task create screen, the modernized create dialog does not use the parent work item's security level for sub-tasks. Instead, it uses the default level of the work item security scheme. If the user is not a member of the default level, the field is left empty and the dialog blocks creation with "Security level is required", even though the user has the Set work item security permission and is a member of the parent's security level. If the user is a member of the default level, the dialog pre-fills and submits the default level. The server ignores it and correctly saves the parent's level, which confirms that only the create dialog is affected. The child work items panel only opens the create dialog when the sub-task work type has other required fields. If Security Level is the only required field, the panel creates the sub-task inline without the dialog, and the sub-task correctly inherits the parent's level. The legacy create experience is not affected. h3. Steps to Reproduce # In a company-managed space, associate a work item security scheme with two levels: *Level A* (scheme default) and *Level B*. # Make the Security Level field *Required* for the Sub-task work type, and add it to the create screen used by Task and Sub-task (shared screen). # Make at least one other field *Required* for the Sub-task work type and add it to the same screen, for example *Components* (create at least one component in the space first). Without another required field, the child work items panel creates the sub-task inline and the problem does not occur. # Grant a non-admin test user the *Set work item security* permission and add them to *Level B* only (not Level A). # Make sure *Settings > System > General Configuration > Simple Create as Default* is *on*. # As the test user, create a Task with security level *Level B*. # From the Task's child work items panel, add a sub-task, enter a summary and select *Create*. The create dialog opens and asks for the required fields. # Fill in the other required field and select *Create*. h3. Expected Results The sub-task is created and inherits the parent's security level (*Level B*), as it does in the legacy create experience. h3. Actual Results The Security Level field is empty and the dialog shows "Security level is required". The sub-task cannot be created. The create metadata ( }) returns } = *Level A* for both an admin and the test user, but } for the test user only contains *Level B*. The dialog therefore has no valid value to pre-fill. For a user who is a member of *Level A*, the dialog submits }} in }. The server returns 201 and saves the sub-task with the parent's level (*Level B*), ignoring the submitted value. No server-side exception is logged; the error is shown as a field validation message in the create dialog. h3. Workaround Either of the following: # Remove the Security Level field from the sub-task create screen, using a dedicated screen for the Sub-task work type in the work type screen scheme. Sub-tasks still inherit the parent's security level on save. # Turn off *Settings > System > General Configuration > Simple Create as Default* to use the legacy create experience. This applies to the entire site.

title: Team field avatar icon displays as grey in the new Jira work item experience despite custom color configured
description: h3. Issue Summary Team field avatar icon displays as grey in the new Jira work item experience despite custom color configured h3. Steps to Reproduce # Ensure a Team has an avatar color or custom icon configured (via Atlassian Home / Teams directory). # Assign or associate this team to a work item using the Team field. # Open the work item using the new work item experience (modern issue view). # Inspect the Team field in the right-hand details/context panel. h3. Expected Results The Team field renders the team's configured avatar and color palette, matching what is displayed in the Team profile and the Team picker dropdown. h3. Actual Results The Team field renders a static, monochrome grey placeholder icon for all teams, disregarding the team's configured color. !screenshot-1.png|thumbnail! h3. Workaround Temporarily switch back to the classic issue experience: Turn off the new work item view via Personal settings (or the in-product view switcher/Labs toggle) to access the classic issue view, where team avatar colors render as expected.

title: Modern Work Item View: Unable to clear/empty "Group Picker (single group)" custom field
description: h3. Issue Summary In the Modern Work Item View (Beta), users are unable to clear the value of a "Group Picker (single group)" custom field once a value has been set. The UI does not provide a way to return the field to an empty state, it only allows switching between existing groups. This functionality works as expected in the legacy issue view. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Enable the *Modern work item view* beta feature. # Navigate to an issue that contains a custom field of type Group Picker (single group) . # Set a value (select a group) for this field and save/confirm. # Attempt to clear the field to make it empty (e.g., by clicking an 'X', deleting the text, or selecting a 'None' option if applicable). # Observe that the value remains or the UI does not allow the field to be saved as empty. h3. Expected Results Users should be able to clear the field value and save it as empty, consistent with the behavior in the legacy issue view. h3. Actual Results The field cannot be cleared. The user can only change the value to a different group, but cannot revert it to an empty state. ... h3. Workaround Disable the "Modern work item view" beta feature and use the old view to clear the field value.
comment: Engineer Note: The Jira engineering team has identified the cause of this issue and fixed the issue. Users who previously experienced issues with group picker should be able to work with the field seamlessly.  If you are currently in an active session, please perform a hard refresh of your browser (Ctrl + F5 or Cmd + Shift + R) to ensure the changes take effect. If you continue to experience any issues with the group picker field, please let us know by commenting on this ticket or contacting Atlassian Support.

title: Clicking the "Driver" field on the Jira Release create/edit screen results in "No options" being displayed for all users.
description: h3. Issue Summary In Jira Cloud, the Driver field within the Release create/edit screen fails to populate any user options, even when no search text is entered. This issue affects all users, including those with Jira Administration permissions. The Assignee field on the same screen functions correctly. Investigation using DevTools reveals a GraphQL error from the DriverFieldQuery indicating a failure to retrieve site admin groups, which prevents the user search parameters from being built correctly. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Navigate to a Jira Software project # Go to Releases in the project sidebar. # Click Create release or open an existing release to edit. # Click on the Driver field to open the user selection dropdown. h3. Expected Results A list of eligible users should be displayed in the dropdown. h3. Actual Results The dropdown displays "No options". h3. Workaround Currently there is no known workaround for this behavior. A workaround will be added here when available

title: Jira Incoming Mail Handler creates duplicate tickets
description: h3. Issue Summary Jira Incoming Mail Handler creates duplicate tickets instead of threading replies when the original email and its reply are processed in the same batch job. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Configure an incoming mail handler (Jira Software or Jira Work Management) with a specific polling interval (e.g., 10 minutes). # Send an original email to the handler's address. # Send a reply to that same email within the same polling window (before the next mail job runs). # Wait for the Jira Incoming Mails job to execute. h3. Expected Results Jira should process the original email first to create a work item, and then process the reply to add it as a comment to that work item. h3. Actual Results The emails are processed in a non-deterministic order. If the reply email is processed before the original email (often due to smaller file size or asynchronous processing), Jira does not find an existing } in the table and creates a second, separate ticket for the reply. h3. Workaround Currently there is no known workaround for this behavior. A workaround will be added here when available.

title: Retry skips failed permission-scheme creation after required groups are synchronized due to stale idempotency tokens
description: h3. Issue Summary During Jira project import, permission-scheme creation can fail when a referenced group is not yet available on the destination site. After the required group is synchronized and the import is retried, the previously failed permission-scheme operation is treated as already processed because of its stored idempotency token. The operation is skipped instead of retried, leaving the affected project without the required permission scheme or in a failed state. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Start a Jira project import where a permission scheme references a group that is not yet available on the destination site. # Allow permission-scheme creation to fail because the required group is missing. # Synchronize or create the required group on the destination site. # Retry the same project import without clearing its existing idempotency state. # Observe that the previously failed permission-scheme operation is skipped. h3. Expected Results A permission-scheme operation that failed because a required group was unavailable remains eligible for retry. After the group becomes available, retrying the import successfully creates the permission scheme. Successfully completed operations remain idempotent and are not duplicated. h3. Actual Results The previously failed permission-scheme operation is treated as already processed because an idempotency token exists. The operation is skipped during the retry, so the permission scheme is not created h3. Workaround Currently, there is no known workaround for this behavior. A workaround will be added here when available A targeted removal of the affected idempotency tokens may permit the import to be retried. This must only be performed using engineering-approved SQL and applicable change controls. A durable code fix is required.

title: Make the statusCategory field consistent in JQL searches (case sensitivity)
description: h3. Issue Summary The behavior of the statusCategory field is inconsistent when querying it via JQL, precisely regarding case sensitivity.  h3. Steps to Reproduce Three scenarios with inconsistent results: h4. Scenario 1 statusCategory = done Works as expected. !image-2026-09-21-16-36-27-873.png|width=244,height=139! h4. Scenario 2 statusCategory = Done Works as expected. !image-2026-09-21-16-35-52-183.png|width=246,height=140! Notice that both queries work, regardless of the capital D on the second one. h4. Scenario 3 Now, if we use the following, it doesn't work: statusCategory = DONE !image-2026-09-21-16-37-55-236.png|width=247,height=141! It doesn't seem to be case-sensitive in the first two queries, but the third fails. h3. Expected Results The query results should be consistent; the field should be either case-sensitive or not. If it is, only the second scenario should work. If it isn't, all should work. h3. Actual Results Inconsistent results as shown above. h3. Workaround Currently, there is no known workaround for this behavior. A workaround will be added here when available.
comment: Engineer Note: Hi everyone, we’ve fixed this issue— statusCategory{}}} values in JQL are now case-insensitive. Thanks for your patience!

title: Bulk move page with many combinations can result in OutOfMemoryError in large instances
description: h3. Summary: JIRA users are able to bulk move issues. When performing this operation the issues will be presented to the user so that they may select the destination. * This selection occurs at "Step 3 of 4: Select Projects and Issue Types" This page will combine issues into groups, allowing a destination to be selected for that group. +Example+: * "You have chosen to move 1000 issues from 8 project(s) with 14 issue type(s). You can either select a new project and issue type for each of the existing 26 combinations below or choose to move all standard issues to a single project and issue type." Each combination provides a project and issue type dropdown. In addition sub-tasks also show a third dropdown for selecting a new parent. * Note: JIRA does not combine sub-tasks into a combination on the bulk move page when those sub-tasks have different parents. h3. Steps to Reproduce * Use very large instance, greater than 2000 projects and issue types * Ensure user performing action has permission for these projects * Attempt bulk move where the set of issues contains a large number of subtasks that have distinct parents ** Example JQL: "issuetype in subTaskIssueTypes()" h3. Problem Behavior: Instances with a large number of projects and issue types may encounter memory issues if a large number of combinations appear. This can result in OutOfMemoryError when rendering the page. h3. Expected Behavior: JIRA prevents the page from causing memory issues. * Perhaps a limit on the number of combinations that can be displayed * Or perhaps the page could be changed to work differently. h3. Additional Details: The presence of sub-tasks in the search results can result in a large number of combinations. JIRA does not combine sub-tasks into a combination on the bulk move page when those sub-tasks have different parents. In one example we found 277 issues returned by the search. Mostly sub-tasks, these resulted in 271 combinations on the bulk move page. * Each of the 271 combinations loaded the following lists: ** Project List = 2590 values, 665135 characters, 650KB ** Issue type List = 3382 values, 985747 characters, 963KB The total for just these lists was over 400MB. The entire BodyContentImpl containing these lists was over 900MB in size. * Five BodyContentImpl objects exist, all related to the bulk move. Total retained heap is around 6GB for these five objects The large objects show in the dominator tree: * !image-2018-03-08-19-07-57-609.png|thumbnail! Heap is consumed by very large Char objects tied to the bulk move: * !image-2018-03-08-19-10-09-524.png|thumbnail! * !image-2018-03-08-19-20-29-319.png|thumbnail!   h3. Workaround Only move one set of (target project, target issue type) issues at a time.
comment: Engineer Note: Workaround is to only move one set of (target proejct, target issue type) issues at a time. I've seen problems trying to do too much in a bulk move as well

title: Users without 'Manage Versions (Releases)' or 'Administer Projects' permissions are allowed to to manage approvers
description: h3. Issue Summary Users who do not possess the 'Manage Versions (Releases)' or 'Administer Projects' project permissions are still able to access release management features. Specifically, unauthorized users can configure/manage release approvers directly from the Releases page. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Configure a project permission scheme such that a test user is only granted the 'Browse Projects' permission (ensure 'Manage Versions (Releases)' and 'Administer Projects' are not granted to the user or any group/role they belong to). # Log in as the test user and navigate to the project's Releases page: https://<instance>.atlassian.net/projects/<PROJECT_KEY>?selectedItem=com.atlassian.jira.jira-projects-plugin:release-page # Test adding/managing approvers for releases. # Run the Permission Helper for the test user to confirm: "User does not have the 'Manage Versions (Releases)' permission" h3. Expected Results Users without 'Manage Versions (Releases)' or 'Administer Projects' permissions should only have a read-only view of the Releases page and should be prevented from modifying approvers. h3. Actual Results The user can assign arbitrary approvers even without the required permissions. The following exception is thrown in the xxxxxxx.log file: N/A (UI and permission evaluation enforcement gap) h3. Workaround Currently, there is no known workaround for this behavior. A workaround will be added here when available.

title: Ampersand in approval custom field name renders as & in issue view approval rule text
description: h3. Issue Summary When an approval step on a workflow status is configured using a custom field that contains an ampersand ( &{}}}) in its name, the approval requirement banner on the issue view HTML-encodes the character and displays literal } instead of &{}}}. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Navigate to *⚙️ Settings > Work Items > Fields* and create a *User Picker (multiple users)* or *Group Picker* custom field with an ampersand in the name (e.g., Chair & Co-Chair Approvers{}}}). # Associate the custom field with the target project's screens. # Navigate to *Space settings > Workflows* and edit the active workflow. # Select a status (e.g., Awaiting approval{}}}), enable Include approval step , and set the approver source to the custom field created in Step 1. # Publish/Update the workflow. # Create an issue, populate the approver field, and transition the issue into the approval status. # Observe the *Approvals* section in the issue view h3. Expected Results The approval requirement rule text properly renders the unescaped ampersand character: } h3. Actual Results The approval requirement rule text HTML-escapes the ampersand character, rendering the raw HTML entity &{}}}: } _(Note: The approval section title itself renders the ampersand cleanly; only the rule/condition sentence exhibits the HTML-escaping issue.)_ h3. Workaround Rename the custom field to use the word *"and"* (e.g., Chair and Co-Chair Approvers{}}})

title: Updating the custom field description in a Team Managed Project does not reflect in the View/Create screen

Steps to Reproduce # Create a custom field in a Team-managed project via Project settings > Fields # Update the description # Add the field to the Work Type # Open Create issue or View issue. # Description is not displayed. h3. title: New CSV Import experience creates unstarted sprints with a completed date, causing HTTP 400 error when starting the sprint
description: h3. Issue Summary New CSV Import experience creates unstarted sprints with a completed date, causing _HTTP 400_ error when starting the sprint. h3. Steps to Reproduce * Prepare or export a CSV file containing issue data with the sprint name. The Sprint is not available on the project itself * In Jira cloud, navigate to project settings/board and import the CSV using the New Import Experience. * Locate the newly created sprint on the backlog board. * Attempt to click Start Sprint and configure the sprint dates later than when the import occurred h3. Expected Results * The CSV import should handle sprint fields cleanly without generating corrupted sprint records. * Newly imported/created sprints that have never been started must not have a completeDate populated. * Users should be able to start the sprint normally without date validation errors. h3. Actual Results * The import creates a new sprint with a completeDate already populated in the backend. * When attempting to start the sprint, the action fails with an HTTP 400 (Bad Request) error: "The start date of a sprint must be before the complete date." h3. Workaround * Recreate the sprint via UI on the board. * Move all issues from the imported sprint into the newly created sprint. * Delete the corrupted imported sprint from the board. * Start the newly created sprint as normal.

title: JQL list view | Configure columns: State information not announced by NVDA
description: h3. Issue Summary NVDA does not announce whether columns are selected or unselected. *Note:* This issue has been raised as "Medium" priority issue since it has a lower user impact, reproducible only with the NVDA screen reader. The functionality works as expected with JAWS and VoiceOver screen readers. h3. Test URL [TestEnv|https://anusooya-1756357433853.atlassian.net/jira/software/projects/JQL/issues?jql=project%20%3D%20%22JQL%22%20ORDER%20BY%20created%20DESC] h3. Steps to Reproduce # Open the Jira Cloud instance and navigate to the issues section # Switch the JQL search interface to list view. # Locate and select the "Configure columns" button within the data table. # Using NVDA screen reader, navigate through the column list with the Down Arrow key. # Observe that NVDA does not announce the selected or unselected state of the columns during navigation. h3. Screen Recording [^JQL_Search_NVDA.mp4] h3. Actual Results When users activate the "Configure columns" button, the dropdown displays both selected and unselected columns. However, NVDA does not announce the selection status as other screen readers do. It only announces the column names when they receive focus or are hovered over, without indicating whether they are selected or unselected. Additionally, users must deselect and then reselect a column for NVDA to announce its state information. This behavior makes it difficult for users relying on the NVDA screen reader to determine the selection status of a column. h3. Expected Results The selected or unselected state must be communicated to all screen reader users during navigation. In this case, ensure that NVDA announces the selected or unselected state of each column by default when it receives focus or when the user hovers over it. Apply the following changes: * Use appropriate ARIA roles and attributes to support multi-selection, such as role="listbox" on the container and aria-multiselectable="true" to indicate multiple selections. * Assign each column item the role role="option" and include the aria-selected attribute with a value of true or false to represent its selection state. * Ensure the aria-selected attribute updates dynamically when a user selects or deselects a column so NVDA can announce the state change immediately. * Allow users to navigate through the list using the Up and Down Arrow keys, and toggle selection using the Space or Enter key. * Verify that NVDA announces each column’s name followed by its selection state, such as “Assignee, selected” or “Reporter, not selected.” * Confirm that NVDA dynamically announces changes in selection, for example, “Priority, selected” or “Priority, not selected.” * Ensure the state information is available both on focus and hover, allowing users to understand the selection status without performing additional actions. h3. Workaround Currently there is no known workaround for this behavior. A workaround will be added here when available. h3. Environment Windows - 11 Pro MacBook Pro - macOs 15.4.1 Chrome - Version 141.0.7390.123 (Official Build) (arm64) Firefox - Version 136.0.4 Safari - Version 18.3 (20620.2.4.11.5) JAWS - Version 2025 NVDA - Version 2024.4.2.35031 Voiceover - Version Latest

title: Forge user list custom field missing from Jira’s “Users in a custom field” workflow condition and permission scheme
description: h3. Issue Summary: * The Forge custom field is defined as  } with  collection: list{}}}. * Jira already recognizes the field as user-typed: ** It appears in  Transition → Conditions → Restrict to when a field is a specific value . ** Jira renders a user picker for the comparison value. ** Jira can read the field’s user values during condition evaluation. * However, the same field is missing from: ** *Transition → Conditions → Restrict who can move a work item → Users in a custom field* ** *Permission schemes → User custom field value* h3. Steps to Reproduce *Prerequisites:* # Create a Forge app with the following manifest module: modules:   jira:customFieldType:     - key: user-list-field-repro       name: User List Repro       type: user       collection: list       formatter:         expression: "value?.map(user => user.displayName ?? user.accountId).join(', ') ?? ''"       view:         resource: view         render: native         experience:           - issue-view       edit:         resource: edit         render: native         experience:           - issue-view # Deploy and install the app on a Jira Cloud site. # Go to  Settings → Issues → Custom Fields → Add custom field . # Select the Forge field type (“User List Repro”) and create a field instance. Add it to a screen. # Set a user value on an issue via the field (confirms the field works and stores user objects correctly). *Reproduce the inconsistency:* # Go to a company-managed project → *Project Settings → Workflows* → Edit a workflow. # Click on a transition → *Add condition* → select  “Restrict to when a field is a specific value” . # Open the *“For this field”* dropdown. ** ✅ *“User List Repro” IS present.* Jira also renders a user picker for the value — confirming it recognizes the field as user-typed. # Cancel. Add another condition → *“Restrict who can move a work item”* →  “Users in a custom field” . # Open the field dropdown. ** ❌ *“User List Repro” is NOT present.* Only native userpicker / multiuserpicker fields appear. # Go to *Settings → Issues → Permission Schemes* → Edit any scheme → *Grant permission* →  “User custom field value” . # Open the field dropdown. ** ❌ *“User List Repro” is NOT present.* *Expected Results* The Forge custom field with  } /  } should appear in *all* Jira UI selectors that accept user-typed fields, including: * ✅ “Restrict to when a field is a specific value” — *already works* * ✅ “Users in a custom field” workflow condition — *currently broken* * ✅ “User custom field value” permission scheme grant — *currently broken* The eligibility filter for these selectors should match by field schema ( schema.type == "user"{}}} or  schema.items == "user"{}}}) rather than by a hardcoded set of native field type keys. h3. Actual Results The Forge user-list custom field appears in some user-field selectors but is completely absent from condition *“Restrict who can move a work item”:* * The *“Users in a custom field”* workflow condition field dropdown * The *“User custom field value”* permission scheme field dropdown The REST API confirms the field schema is correct and identical in shape to a native multi-user-picker: GET /rest/api/3/field } h3. Workaround Currently there is no known workaround for this behavior. A workaround will be added here when available
comment: Engineer Note: Hi all, We have just finished rolling out some changes to include Forge fields for selection in the *Restrict who can move a work item* rule. Thank you for raising the issue. Please let us know if any ongoing issues persist.

title: worklogs with NULL value after migration breaks reports
description: h3. Issue Summary _Sprint Report and Burndown Chart fail with HTTP 500 NumberFormatException when Time Tracking is enabled due to empty WorklogId in changeitem_ h3. title: "Add agent" button is displayed in the workflow editor even when Rovo access is blocked for Jira
description: h3. Issue Summary In Jira Cloud, organization admins can block Rovo for specific apps from *Atlassian Administration > AI and Rovo > Rovo access* (Blocklist). When an app is on the blocklist, Rovo features are expected to be hidden from end users in that app. However, when Rovo access is blocked for Jira, the *"Add agent"* button in the workflow editor toolbar is still displayed. This happens even though the *"Trigger agent"* rule is correctly hidden from the *"Add rule"* options. If users click the "Add agent" button, they cannot select an agent, so they can't complete the action. As a result, users who can edit workflows see a Rovo feature that admins have intentionally blocked, and the button leads nowhere. This causes confusion and raises concerns for organizations that need to restrict AI features in Jira. h3. Steps to Reproduce *Steps:* # As an organization admin, go to Atlassian Administration > AI and Rovo > Rovo access . # On the Blocklist , select Add app , select *Jira* for the site, then select Block access . # Confirm that Jira is shown on the blocklist. # Wait a few minutes for the setting to take effect, then hard-refresh the browser. # In Jira, go to *Space settings > Workflows* and select *Edit workflow* for any workflow. # Check the toolbar at the top of the workflow editor. # Select the *"Add agent"* button. # For comparison, select a transition, select "Add rule" , and check whether the *"Trigger agent"* rule is listed. h3. Expected Results * Because Rovo access is blocked for Jira, no Rovo features are displayed in Jira. * The *"Add agent"* button is not displayed in the workflow editor toolbar, in the same way that the *"Trigger agent"* rule is not displayed in the *"Add rule"* options. h3. Actual Results * The *"Add agent"* button is still displayed in the workflow editor toolbar. * When the button is selected, no agent can be selected, so users can't complete the action. * The *"Trigger agent"* rule is correctly hidden from the *"Add rule"* options. h3. Workaround Currently there is no known workaround for this behavior. A workaround will be added here when available.

title: Pasting an image into the Rovo Chat input field while viewing a work item in Microsoft Edge attaches the image to the work item before the message is sent
description: h3. Issue Summary When a Jira work item is open in Microsoft Edge and an image is pasted from the clipboard into the Rovo Chat input field, the same image is added as an attachment to the work item displayed in the background, even though the Rovo Chat message has not been sent. * Affected browser: Microsoft Edge (Windows / macOS) * Not affected: Google Chrome, Firefox * Space type tested: Company-managed space (software) h3. Steps to Reproduce # Open Jira Cloud in Microsoft Edge and navigate to a board in a company-managed software space # Click any work item on the board to open it # Open Rovo Chat by clicking "Ask Rovo" in the top-right corner # Copy an image to the clipboard (e.g. on macOS, press Cmd + Ctrl + Shift + 4 to save a screenshot to the clipboard) # Click the Rovo Chat input field and paste the image (macOS: Cmd + V / Windows: paste from clipboard history with Win + V) # Do not send the message h3. Expected Results The image is added only to the Rovo Chat input field. It is not attached to the work item displayed in the background. h3. Actual Results At the same time the image is added to the Rovo Chat input field, it is also added as an attachment to the work item displayed in the background. A notification indicating that an attachment was added to the work item is displayed, and the image appears in the work item's Attachments section. The Rovo Chat message has not been sent. When the same steps are performed in Google Chrome, the image is added only to the Rovo Chat input field and is not attached to the work item. h3. Workaround Use Google Chrome or Firefox when pasting images into Rovo Chat. The image will not be attached to the work item. Any image that was attached unintentionally can be deleted manually from the work item's Attachments section.

title: Cumulative Flow Report in Team managed projects does not return new data
description: h3. Issue Summary The cumulative flow report stops updating with any recent data. It will appear as if there is no new data after a particular date. New column changes are not being reflected in the report. Applying date filters does not help. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Have a team managed project # Have more than 40,000 issue +*column* *transitions*+ in the projects board Note: Column transitions is distinct from issue status transitions/changes, i.e. multiple statuses can be mapped to a single column in the board config. They are related concepts in that issue status changes lead to issue column changes, but a status change does not always result in a column change. h3. Actual Results The report stops updating with recent data. Applying date filters does not help. h3. Expected Results Users should be able to see either... * All column changes for all time * OR be able to apply filters to exclude old issue data Such that they are able to continue to see new column transitions in the report. h3. Workaround Currently there is no known workaround for this behavior. A workaround will be added here when available. h3. More details The network request to fetch column transition is limited to 40,000 records. Once this limit is reached, no new data will appear in the report as the results are sorted from oldest -> newest then capped at 40,000. The date filters do not help unfortunately as they are client side filters only i.e. the report still attempts to fetch the entire data set which is subject to the 40,000 limit.
comment: Engineer Note: A fix is now available for the issue affecting Cumulative Flow Diagram reports that exceed the default 40,000-record limit. The default limit remains unchanged. title: Site Optimizer: "Select project" dropdown in Scheme Variant flow is limited to 50 results and search/filter does not work.
description: *Summary:* Site Optimizer: "Select project" dropdown in Scheme Variant flow is limited to 50 results and search/filter does not work.   *Description:* In the Jira Site Optimizer, when an administrator attempts to create a Scheme Variant from the Default Field Scheme optimisation page, they are unable to find or select projects that fall outside the first 50 results returned by the UI. *Technical Root Cause:* * The "Select project" dropdown is limited to a maximum of 50 projects. * The frontend sends a } parameter (e.g., ?query=VAPT{}}}) to the /projects}} endpoint. * The backend API does not currently support or respect the } parameter for filtering by project name or key. title: Cannot update Space Owner or Default Assignee field on newly created spaces when unassigned issues are disabled globally
description: h3. Issue Summary When "Allow unassigned issues" is disabled globally in Jira Cloud, creating a new space/project sets or locks the Space Owner (to the user that created the space) and the Default Assignee field to "Unassigned", preventing the user from updating the default assignee directly. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Navigate to Settings (cog icon) > System > General configuration . # Click *Edit Settings* and set *Allow unassigned issues* to OFF , then click Save . # Create a new space / project. # Check the space settings for *Space Owner / Project Lead* and Default Assignee . # Attempt to change or update the Space Owner / Default Assignee. h3. Expected Results The new space should inherit a valid user as the Project Lead/Space Owner, and the Default Assignee should default to the Project Lead without being set to "Unassigned". title: Upgrading to Jira 10 causes performance degradation in Module Registaration
description: h3. Issue Summary The ScriptRunner’s Fragments Locator feature experienced a significant slowdown from Jira 9 to Jira 10 - registration time has gone from about 2 seconds in Jira 9 to 20+ seconds in Jira 10+.We have recently been looking at ways to improve this. The extra processing time seems related to the plugin API changes in Jira 10, where dom4j was replaced by OsgiPluginXmlDescriptorParser, and every fragment now requires a condition class. As a result, each dynamicModuleDescriptorFactory.loadModules() call is noticeably slower (~1.5 ms per fragment in Jira 9 vs ~21 ms in Jira 10). The additional processing time leads to a poor customer experience, risks HTTP timeouts, and blocks the HTTP thread during registration. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Admin enables Fragment Locator via UI toggle # System discovers all possible fragment locations (typically 500-2000 web sections + 200-500 web panel locations) # For each location, we: ## Generate XML descriptor string (always including the condition element with class attribute) ## Parse XML using OsgiPluginXmlDescriptorParser.parseChildModulesFromSource() to get Element objects ## Call dynamicModuleDescriptorFactory.loadModules(plugin, element) for each location # Atlassian’s API handles the module registration internally h3. Expected Results Loading large amounts of modules should not cause performance degradation. h3. Actual Results Baseline performance on Jira 10 to load 500-2000 web sections + 200-500 web panel locations is 21s h3. Workaround Currently there is no known workaround for this behavior. A workaround will be added here when available

title: Field configuration scheme creation doesn't check for previous unlinked entries in nodeassociation
description: Dear Customers, We're happy to announce that this issue is fixed in Jira } *Before the fix:* deleting a field configuration scheme could leave links from projects to the deleted scheme. If a new scheme later received the same ID, the project appeared to use two schemes and failed with Passed List had more than one value{}}}. One affected project could break search and the scheme admin pages for the whole instance. *What is fixed:* * Jira removes leftover links when a scheme is created or copied, and when a scheme is assigned to a project. Each repair is shown to administrators and written to the audit log. * One broken project no longer breaks search and the scheme admin pages. The broken project is skipped, and the log names it. * An administrator can repair a broken project from the browser, without database access. *What remains:* projects that were already broken before the upgrade are not repaired automatically, because Jira can't know which scheme is correct. An administrator chooses the scheme once. See _"Manual fix for an already broken project (administrator, from the browser)" section below_ For more details please see this [KB article|https://support.atlassian.com/jira/kb/repair-field-configuration-scheme-links-in-jira-data-center-jraserver-79561/]. Best regards, Jakub Reczycki Software Engineer, Jira DC h3. Issue Summary When a Field configuration scheme is created, it doesn't check for previous unlinked entries in nodeassociation. This has a chance creating duplicated entries in the database, if those unlinked entries have an ID that matches the ID of the new field configuration scheme. Duplicate entries cause the field configuration scheme cache to fail loading, leading to severe failures in Jira, including loading issues, searches and reindexing. (i) We couldn't identify any way to cause this condition just by using Jira normally - that would involve either database manipulation or a third-party plugin to create such entries. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Create a few projects # Navigate to ⚙ _> Issues > Field Configuration Schemes_ # Create a new Field configuration scheme called "REPRO-SCHEME" and one called "REPRO-SCHEME-B" # Get its ID by running the query SELECT id, name FROM fieldlayoutscheme WHERE name = 'REPRO-SCHEME'; # Navigate to the projects' field settings and associate them to the new field config scheme # Run this script using Scriptrunner console, replacing } for the ID found in step 4. import com.atlassian.jira.component.ComponentAccessor def flm = ComponentAccessor.getFieldLayoutManager() def scheme = flm.getMutableFieldLayoutScheme(ID_FROM_STEP_4_QUERY) scheme.remove() # Re-assign the projects to "REPRO-SCHEME-B" # Rewind the sequence to the value for the first field configuration scheme: UPDATE sequence_value_item SET seq_id = ID_FROM_STEP_4_QUERY WHERE seq_name = 'FieldLayoutScheme'; # Create a Service project, or create a new field configuration scheme h3. Expected Results The field configuration scheme is either created without issues. In the worst case, it should fail with an error describing the reason. h3. Actual Results The field configuration scheme is created, but Jira becomes unusable due to the duplicated entry that was created. Verify the errors in the logs when trying to perform searches or reindexes: 2026-10-13 19:05:14,222-0300 http-nio-40326-exec-2 url: /j10326/internal-error ERROR [c.a.j.web.servlet.InternalServerErrorServlet] h3. Workaround h4. (Since 10.3.27) Manual fix for an already broken project (administrator, from the browser) Projects that were already broken before the upgrade are not repaired automatically. Such a project is linked to two or more existing field configuration schemes, and Jira can't know which one is correct, so an administrator has to choose. Typical signs: the project's issues fail to open, or } shows } (or } on versions without the fix). # Find the project's ID. Open *Project settings* for the project and look for } or } in the address bar. # Open this address in your browser (as a Jira administrator): https://<your-jira>/secure/admin/SelectFieldLayoutScheme!default.jspa?projectId=<project ID> The shortcut *Project settings > Fields > Use a different scheme* does not open for a broken project, so use the direct address above. # No scheme is selected yet; this is expected. Choose the scheme the project should use, or System Default Field Configuration , then save. Jira removes all of the project's old links, keeps the one you chose, and updates every node in the cluster. # *Re-index the project.* This is required, because issues indexed while the project was broken may be missing from search. h4. (Before 10.3.27) Manual fix for an already broken project (database queries) If you face the error mentioned: * Identify the offending projects and associated schemes: SELECT p.pkey, p.pname, na.source_node_id AS project_id, na.sink_node_id AS scheme_id, fls.name AS scheme_name, fls.description FROM nodeassociation na JOIN project p ON p.id = na.source_node_id LEFT JOIN fieldlayoutscheme fls ON fls.id = na.sink_node_id WHERE na.source_node_entity = 'Project' AND na.sink_node_entity = 'FieldLayoutScheme' AND na.association_type = 'ProjectScheme' AND na.source_node_id IN ( SELECT na2.source_node_id FROM nodeassociation na2 JOIN fieldlayoutscheme f2 ON f2.id = na2.sink_node_id WHERE na2.source_node_entity = 'Project' AND na2.sink_node_entity = 'FieldLayoutScheme' AND na2.association_type = 'ProjectScheme' GROUP BY na2.source_node_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1) ORDER BY p.pkey, na.sink_node_id; * Take a database backup as a precaution * Remove the duplicate entries: DELETE FROM nodeassociation WHERE source_node_entity='Project' AND sink_node_entity='FieldLayoutScheme' AND association_type='ProjectScheme' AND source_node_id = 10100 -- the project AND sink_node_id <> 10200; -- the scheme you want to KEEP To verify if there are lingering entries in the database, which are not causing issues: -- Entries without a valid Field configuration scheme (should be empty) SELECT * FROM nodeassociation na LEFT JOIN fieldlayoutscheme f ON f.id = na.sink_node_id WHERE na.sink_node_entity = 'FieldLayoutScheme' AND f.id IS NULL; Let’s check if there are entries with IDs higher than the current sequence ID: -- No entries in the other queries should be higher than these ones SELECT seq_name, seq_id FROM sequence_value_item WHERE seq_name = 'FieldLayoutScheme'; SELECT MAX(id) FROM fieldlayoutscheme; Just to double-check - query to verify if there are entries with IDs higher than they should in the nodeassociation table -- Entries with IDs higher than expected (should be empty) SELECT na.* FROM nodeassociation na LEFT JOIN fieldlayoutscheme f ON f.id = na.sink_node_id WHERE na.sink_node_entity = 'FieldLayoutScheme' AND f.id IS NULL AND na.sink_node_id >= (SELECT seq_id FROM sequence_value_item WHERE seq_name = 'FieldLayoutScheme');

title: Changing space type in the new work item create screen causes summary and description fields to be cleared
description: h3. Issue Summary The old work item create screen would retain data entered for common fields if you switched to a different space type mid-creation. That is, changing from creating a Task in a Company-managed software space to a Task in a Jira Service Management space after you have filled in certain fields would retain the data entered into those fields. With the current rollout of the new work item create screen, the data in these fields will be wiped if you switch the space type and as a result the work item type being created. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Start creating a new work item via the Global create button # Ensure you have the new work item create screen enabled # Start by creating a Task in a company-managed software space # Fill in the summary, description and/or any other fields # Use the space and task switcher at the top of the create screen to change the work item being created to a Jira Service Management Task h3. Expected Results The data entered in the summary, description or other fields is retained h3. Actual Results Any data entered before the space type was updated is wiped h3. Workaround Currently, there is no known workaround for this behaviour. A workaround will be added here when available

title: Unable to create an outgoing mail server without a username or without a password.
description: h3. Issue Summary When trying to create an outgoing mail server that does not contain a username of password, the authentication will fail when testing the connection even though the SMTP Mail Server does not require a username and password combination. Rather than not attempting auth, Jira attempts auth using fabricated details - the username and password corresponding to the OS level Jira service account name. h3. Steps to Reproduce Have a mail server that uses } (extended hello), advertises authentication (sends an } header) but doesn't require it to send mail. Steps to replicate this using } are available in [JRASERVER-78939|https://jira.atlassian.com/browse/JRASERVER-78939] - Configure an outgoing mail server with the parameters below: -- Service Provider : Custom -- Protocol : SMTPS -- Hostname : smtp.gmail.com (or use a custom SMTP Mail Server of your choice) -- SMTP Port : 465 -- Username : (keep empty) -- Password : (keep empty) !MailServerConfig.png|thumbnail! - Test the connection   (i) Make sure that the Mail Server that you are using does not need a username/password combination to login. h3. Expected Results Mail connection test succeeds. h3. Actual Results Mail server connection fails and cannot be added. h3. Note 1 On further inspection the change password flag is passed in the verify mail server request: name: test description: test from: test@gmail.com prefix: Jira serviceProvider: custom protocol: smtps serverName: smtp.gmail.com port: 465 timeout: 10000 authenticationMethod: password username: test@gmail.com changePassword: true type: smtp   This results in a failure when trying to verify the connection, as it expects a password to be provided: WRMCB = function(e) } ; try )(WRM.I18n.km); define("jira/mail/email", ["exports", "jquery"], function(c, a) ).change(); var f = a("#originalUsername").val(); a("input[name\x3dusername]").bind("change input", function() ) } } ; c.verifyServerConnection = function(b, d) ; a(c.dialogInitializer) }); AJS.namespace("JIRA.app.admin.email", null, require("jira/mail/email")); } catch (e) ; h3. Note 2 The bug is coming from the Java Mail Library that Jira uses to connect to the Mail Server. Basically, what happens when Jira tests the SMTP server connection is the following: - The Java Mail library sends a EHLO command to ask the SMTP server for more information about its capabilities, what it supports, etc... EHLO bb3f49c371fa - The SMTP server responds that it supports the AUTH methods below: DEBUG SMTP: Found extension "AUTH", arg "LOGIN PLAIN XOAUTH2 PLAIN-CLIENTTOKEN OAUTHBEARER XOAUTH" - The Java Mail library (used by Jira) sees that the SMTP Mail Server supports AUTH, and tries to authenticate using the Jira Service Account as the username and some password, even though no username/password combination was provided in the Outgoing Mail form . In a lot of cases, *jira* is used as the service account running Jira, so it will be very common to see "jira" as the user: DEBUG SMTP: protocolConnect login, host=smtp.gmail.com, user=jira, password=<non-null> DEBUG SMTP: Attempt to authenticate using mechanisms: LOGIN PLAIN DIGEST-MD5 NTLM XOAUTH2 - Ultimately, the login fails since an incorrect username/password is passed while the SMTP mail server was not expected any h3. Workaround Add the following JVM parameters to your *setenv.sh* file and then proceed with a restart of Jira (you can find detailed instructions [here|https://confluence.atlassian.com/adminjiraserver/setting-properties-and-options-on-startup-938847831.html]): h4. In case SMTP is used as the protocol in the Outgoing Mail Configuration -Dmail.smtp.ehlo=false -Dmail.smtp.auth=false Notes: - mail.smtp.ehlo=false will prevent java from trying to connect and issue a EHLO command to connect to the mail system - mail.smpt.auth=false will reinforce no authentication to your smtp system. h4. In case SMTPS is used as the protocol in the Outgoing Mail Configuration -Dmail.smtps.ehlo=false -Dmail.smtps.auth=false   Note: - mail.smtps.ehlo=false will prevent java from trying to connect and issue a EHLO command to connect to the mail system - mail.smpts.auth=false will reinforce no authentication to your smtp system.
comment:
Engineer Note: Our mail server is self-hosted MS Exchange
Engineer Note: We're running Jira 10.3.22 and this is still an issue. In our case it was sufficient to add  -Dmail.smtps.ehlo=false  to work around the problem.

title: The error message provided on failures when setting the application (incoming - 3rd Party apps) is inconsistent with reality.
description: h2. Description  The error message provided on failures when setting the application (incoming - 3rd Party apps) doesn't display the real error message, causing confusion to users, and for troubleshooting purposes, currently the message seems to be +*hardcoded*+ blindly stating all fields need to be filled out, even when they are all filled out, but really error message (HAR file) is different. h2. Version info - Found in *10.3.5* - Still happening at *10.3.6* h3. Steps to Reproduce # Install Jira 10.3.5, setup _server.xml_ file missing the required _secure=true_ parameter # Try to create an incoming 3rd-party link # Fill in all the fields # Jira will display an error stating: " Fill in required fields and try again ". h3. Expected Results * Jira should not have a hardcoded message because it will mislead the real output of what is occurring; better descriptive messages should be displayed to guide users and support, or even at least, display the real one as same as we see in HAR file " Please ensure that your server is using HTTPS and that your application base URL is configured appropriately. " this could guide users and support to double-check any _connector_ configuration mismatches. ], "cookies": [], "content": }" }, h3. Actual Results * Jira displays a message that doesn't fit with reality. !Screenshot 2025-05-30 at 10.59.14.png!   h3. Workaround *+For the blocking issue it causes:+* Edit the current connector and set the missing and required parameter for OAuth: [Running Jira applications over SSL or HTTPS|https://confluence.atlassian.com/adminjiraserver/running-jira-applications-over-ssl-or-https-938847764.html#:~:text=100%22%20scheme%3D%22https%22-,secure%3D%22true%22,-sslEnabledProtocols%3D%22TLSv1.2%2CTLSv1.3] it will bypass the error and allow application link to be saved. *+For the error message:+* None
comment: Engineer Note: Running oauth2 provider system over http is possible by setting the system property "atlassian.oauth2.provider.skip.base.url.https.requirement" to "true", described here: https://confluence.atlassian.com/adminjiraserver102/oauth-2-0-provider-system-properties-1473876273.html

title: Webhook historian causes primary key constraint violation in Data Center products
description: h3. Issue Summary Since Jira Data Center 10.0 (Atlassian Webhooks 6.1+), webhook invocation history (headers/body/timing) and counts (success/failures/errors) are stored in the } and } database tables, respectively. This functionality primarily exists for Bitbucket DC and Confluence DC, but the data can still be queried from Jira's database for troubleshooting and statistics. In customer environments with extraordinary webhook usage, concurrent non-atomic operations may attempt to update the } table simultaneously. While this does not impact webhook delivery and is typically self-repairing, this produces log errors and may mildly skew statistics. h3. Steps to Reproduce Atlassian Support hasn't successfully reproduced this behavior. It was directly observed in a customer's environment with ~300 webhook configurations and 65k users. h3. title: Project list within the Service Account created limited to 1000 results
description: h3. Issue Summary Can't find all projects in the Resource selection within the Service Account creation. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Have more than 1000 projects in the environment # Create a Service Account # On the "Select resources" page, search for projects that, alphabetically, go beyond the 1000 limit h3. When looking at the HAR file, we see that this request is limited to 1000 results: * Page request with the limit /rest/service-accounts/latest/resources?resource-type-id=project&query=&start=0&limit=1000 h3. Workaround If you need to associate specific projects to an account, you can create the Service Account through Rest, using the following endpoint: } } , \ ] }}} This will allow you to define the projects, even if the initial search can't find them.

title: Native Project Picker Dropdown Clipped in Create Dialog
description: h3. Issue Summary When creating an issue,the project select list exceeds the height of the Create Issue pop-up when the create screen has few fields, making it difficult to scroll to and select projects at the bottom of the list. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Spin up a Jira instance on version 11.3.10. # Ensure there are 50 or more projects. # Configure the create screen to have very few fields (so the project dropdown list extends beyond the visible screen area). # Open the issue create dialog and attempt to scroll down and select a project near the bottom of the list. h3. Expected Results The project select list should be scrollable within the pop-up, allowing all projects to be accessible regardless of how many fields are on the create screen. h3. Actual Results When the create screen has few fields, the project select list overflows the screen, making it difficult to scroll to and click projects at the bottom of the list. h3. Workaround Add more fields to the create screen. This reduces the height of the project list pop-up, making all projects selectable.

title: Bullet list formatting from Microsoft Word is not preserved when pasted into a Jira comment.

title: URL Custom Fields appear blank in the UI for existing file:// values after upgrading Jira
description: h3. Issue Summary Following the upgrade to Jira 11.3.10, URL custom fields that previously contained } links no longer display those values in the Jira UI (. While the data remains intact in the } database table, the new URL validation layer  treats these existing values as invalid and returns } to the display layer. This results in a perceived data loss for customers who rely on these fields to reference local or network resources. h3. Steps to Reproduce * On a Jira version prior to 11.3.10 (e.g., 11.3.8), create a URL Custom Field . * Create an issue and populate the field with a } link (e.g., file:https://server/path/document.pdf{}}}). * Upgrade the Jira instance to version 11.3.10 . * View the issue created in Step 2. h3. Expected Results The existing } value should be displayed in the UI, even if the scheme is now restricted for _new_ inputs. h3. Actual Results * The URL field appears completely *blank* in the Issue View. * The REST API returns a } value for the field. * CSV and XML exports omit the value. * *Note:* A direct database query confirms the data still exists in the } table. h3. Workaround Currently there is no known workaround for this behavior. A workaround will be added here when available
comment: Engineer Note: This is fixed in Jira 11.3.13 . The fix for the 10.3 line is merged and will ship in the next 10.3 bug-fix release.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  *Affected versions:* 11.3.9 to 11.3.12 and 10.3.24 to 10.3.26. The problem started in 11.3.9, not 11.3.10.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    *What the fix does*                                                                                                                                                                                                                       * The URL scheme check now runs only when someone enters a new value. Values that are already stored are no longer checked when the issue is read. Existing } values (and any other scheme not on the list) appear again in     the issue view, in the REST API, and in CSV and XML exports. The data in } was never lost.                                                               * Editing an unrelated field on an issue that has one of these values no longer fails validation.                                                                                             * A stored value whose scheme is not on the list is shown as plain text, not as a clickable link.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    *Keeping [file://|file:///] links clickable*                                                                                                                                                                                                     From 11.3.13 the list of accepted schemes is configurable. A system administrator can change it in  Administration > System > General configuration > Advanced settings , key jira.customfield.url.allowed.schemes{}}}. Add } to   the comma-separated list. No restart is needed. The setting also lets users enter new } values.                                                                                                                               Only add  } if your organization needs it. } links point at the local or network file system of whoever clicks them, which is why the scheme is not on the default list.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              *Workaround for 11.3.9 to 11.3.12 and 10.3.24 to 10.3.26*                                                                                                                                                     No configuration workaround exists on these versions because the list cannot be changed there. Upgrade to 11.3.13, or to the next 10.3 bug-fix release once it is out.

title: Issue Security Level incorrectly resets to the scheme's default value when a workflow transition fails a validator
description: h3. Issue Summary A regression introduced in Jira 10.0.0 causes the *Security Level* of an issue to be automatically updated to the security scheme's default value if a workflow transition fails a validator (e.g., a required field validator). This occurs even though the transition is not completed and the issue's Security Level was previously set to "None" (unset). When the transition screen is redisplayed after the validation error, Jira falls back to the default security level instead of maintaining the current "None" state. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Install Jira Software or Jira Service Management version 10.0.0 or later (11.3.10 as of writing this) # Create a project and configure an *Issue Security Scheme* with a specific level set as the Default . # Create a workflow transition that includes a *Validator* and screen during transition (e.g., "Field Required" or "administration access" validator). # Create an issue and ensure the *Security Level* is set to None . # Attempt to perform the transition without filling in the required field to trigger a validator failure. # Observe the Security Level field on the redisplayed transition screen. h3. Expected Results The transition fails with a validation error, and the *Security Level* remains unchanged as None . h3. Actual Results The transition fails with a validation error, but the *Security Level* is automatically populated with the *Default Security Level* from the scheme. If the user then fills the required field and completes the transition, the Security Level is updated to the default value without the user's explicit intent.   h3. Workaround Remove the *Default Security Level* from the Issue Security Scheme configuration. This ensures that if a transition fails, there is no default value for Jira to fall back to, preserving the "None" state.

title: Two dimensional filter statistics gadget does not show empty (none) values
description: h3. Issue Summary The *Two Dimensional Filter Statistics* gadget does not show empty (none) values It affects Jira Data Center 11.0.0 and later (symptoms are slightly different in 11.3.10 and later) h3. Steps to Reproduce # Create a test project. # Create a test custom field with the *Checkboxes* type and three options ( A , *B* and C ), adding it to all the test project’s screens. # Perform a full re-index. # Create four issues in the test project, as follows: ## The first issue should have the test custom field set to A . ## The second issue should have the test custom field set to B . ## The third issue should have the test custom field set to C . ## The fourth issue should have the test custom field left blank (no options selected). # Create a saved search filter that returns only the four newly created issues (e.g. project = <test project key>). # Add a *Two Dimensional Filter Statistics* gadget to the Jira dashboard and configure it as follows: ## *Saved Filter* should be set to the search filter created in step 4. ## *XAxis* should be set to the test custom field created in step 2. ## *YAxis* can be set to Assignee , *Status* or some other field. # If the Jira version is 11.3.10 or later, edit the test issue from step 3.1 and set the test custom field to A + B . h3. Expected Results There should be four columns ( A , B , *C* and None ), and the *Total* column’s value should be the sum of the four columns' values. h3. Actual Results The *None* column is missing, and the *Total* column’s value does not match the sum of the three displayed columns' values. h3. Workaround No workaround is available

title: Clone dialog in the new work item view doesn't include attachments and links options
description: h3. Issue Summary Clone dialog in the new work item view doesn't show the Include options (Attachments, Links) when the work item has attachments and links. h3. Steps to Reproduce In a Jira Cloud site where the new work item view is turned on , open a work item that has at least one attachment added directly to it and at least one work item link to another work item. # Make sure the work item is open in the new work item view. # Select More actions (•••) > Clone. # Check the Clone dialog. h3. Expected Results The Clone dialog shows the _Include_ section with the _Attachments_ and _Links_ checkboxes, as it does in the classic work item view. Users can choose to copy attachments and links to the cloned work item, as described in [Clone a work item|https://support.atlassian.com/jira-software-cloud/docs/clone-an-issue/]. h3. Actual Results The Clone dialog only shows Summary , _Assignee_ and Reporter . The _Include_ section (Attachments / Links) is missing, so attachments and links can't be copied to the cloned work item. h3. Workaround # *Per user (no admin needed):* On the work item, select ••• (More actions) > Switch to classic view , then use Clone . The Attachments and Links options are available there, as you saw. This only changes the view for that user. # *For the whole site (admin):* Go to Settings > System > General configuration > Edit settings , turn off New work item view , and select Update . All users will go back to the classic view, and you can turn it back on at any time.

title: Modern Create experience - Enter key does not insert line breaks in custom Paragraph fields
description: h3. Issue Summary In the new Jira Cloud Create experience, pressing Enter in custom Paragraph (multiline rich-text) fields does not insert a line break. The issue affects fields such as Actual Results, Expected Results, and Steps to Reproduce. The same fields accept and preserve multiple lines in the legacy Create experience, forcing the customer to disable the modern experience site-wide. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Configure a Jira Cloud project with one or more custom Paragraph fields on the Create screen. # Enable the modern Create experience by setting Simple Create as Default to On. # Open the Create dialog and select an issue type containing the custom Paragraph fields. # Enter text in a Paragraph field, press Enter, and enter additional text. # Repeat with fields such as Actual Results, Expected Results, or Steps to Reproduce. h3. Expected Results Pressing Enter in a custom Paragraph field should create a new line, allowing users to enter multiline content during issue creation. The resulting issue should preserve the line breaks. h3. Actual Results Pressing Enter does not create a new line in custom Paragraph fields in the modern Create experience. Entered text remains on a single line or is collapsed together. The behavior is specific to the modern Create experience: * The same fields support multiline input in the legacy Create experience. * Jira's standard Description field supports multiline input during creation. * Editing an existing issue allows multiline input in the affected custom fields. h3. Workaround Set Simple Create as Default to Off under Settings > System > General Configuration to revert to the legacy Create experience. The customer confirmed that this restores multiline input functionality. As a secondary workaround, users may create the issue with single-line content and add line breaks later from the issue's Edit view.

title: Hyperlink click prompts discard dialog instead of opening link when create screen has unsaved field values
description: h3. Issue Summary When a user has entered values into one or more fields on the global create form, clicking an existing hyperlink no longer opens the target URL directly. Instead, the app prompts the user to discard changes or go back, forcing them to use a right-click/open-in-new-tab workaround. This creates inconsistent behaviour compared to the same link when the form is unmodified, and it interrupts users who have partially completed the form. h3. Steps to Reproduce * Select the global Create option that contains a hyperlink. * Verify that clicking the hyperlink works normally when no fields have been edited. * Enter a value into one or more fields on the create screen * Click the same hyperlink again. * Observe that the app prompts to discard changes or go back instead of opening the link. * Optionally discard changes and navigate back, then click the link again to confirm it works once the form is no longer dirty. h3. Expected Results * Clicking a hyperlink should behave consistently regardless of whether the form has unsaved field values. h3. Actual Results * The app prompts to discard changes or go back instead of opening the link. h3. Workaround * Users can right click and open in a new tab as a workaround

title: Capacity Planning CSV import does not recognise contributors by email address
description: h3. Issue Summary Capacity Planning CSV imports can fail to recognise existing contributors when the file identifies them by email address. Replacing the email address with the same person’s display name allows the contributor to be matched. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Select an existing user who is accessible on the Jira site. # Prepare a Capacity Planning CSV using that user’s email address in the contributor column and otherwise valid import data. # Import the CSV into a capacity plan. # Repeat with the same data, replacing only the email address with the user’s display name. h3. Expected Results The import can recognise accessible contributors by email address as well as by name, and produces suggestions for review. h3. Actual Results The email-based lookup can return no matching contributor, while the name-based lookup succeeds. Unmatched contributors are omitted from suggestions. When no usable data remains, the import can display “We couldn’t complete your request”. h3. Workaround Use the contributor’s display name instead of their email address and review the suggested people before accepting the import, especially where multiple people share a name.

title: Timeline view only displays first 50 Quick Filters from board configuration
description: h3. Issue Summary The Timeline view in company-managed projects only displays the first 50 Quick Filters from the board configuration. Any filters beyond the 50th position are missing from the Timeline UI, even though they are visible and functional on the Kanban board. h3. Steps to Reproduce * Create a Kanban board in a company-managed project. * Add more than 50 Quick Filters to the board configuration. * Navigate to the Timeline view. * Observe that only the first 50 filters are visible. * Reorder a filter from position 16+ to the top 50 and observe it appearing in Timeline. h3. Expected Results The Timeline view should display all Quick Filters available on the board, or at least match the board's capability (which fetches up to 50). h3. Actual Results The Timeline view is strictly capped at 50 Quick Filters. Filters beyond this limit are hidden unless reordered to be within the top 50. h3. Workaround Keep essential Quick Filters within the top 50 positions in the board's Quick Filter settings.

title: "CSV - my defaults" export ignores user-configured columns and reverts to system defaults
description: h3. Issue Summary When a user configures a specific set of columns under the *"My defaults"* tab in the column picker within the issue search, the *"Export CSV - my defaults"* (and Excel CSV equivalent) fails to respect these selections. Instead, the exported file consistently contains only a standard set of system default fields, regardless of which custom or system fields the user has added or removed in the UI. This issue affects all custom field types and prevents users from obtaining a tailored export based on their saved personal preferences. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Navigate to Filters > Search work items . # *Search* for a few work items # Click on the *Columns* button. # Under the *My defaults* tab, add several custom fields (e.g., Paragraph, Radio Buttons, Select Lists) and remove some standard system fields (e.g., Priority, Due Date). # Click ••• > *Export* in the top right corner. # Select *Export Excel CSV - my defaults* or Export CSV - my defaults . # Open the resulting CSV file. h3. Expected Results The exported CSV should contain exactly the columns configured in the "My defaults" UI view at the time of export. h3. Actual Results The CSV contains a hardcoded set of system default fields, ignoring the user's configuration: * Work type (Issue Type) * Work item key (Key) * Summary * Priority * Assignee * Reporter * Status * Resolution * Created * Updated * Due date h3. Workaround Use the *"Export CSV - all fields"* option. This will include all available fields in the instance, including the desired custom fields. Users can then manually delete the unnecessary columns in their spreadsheet application.

title: Jira Plans PNG export hangs indefinitely when using custom icons hosted as Confluence attachments
description: h3. Issue Summary When attempting to export a Jira Plan timeline view as a PNG image ( Share > Export > Export an image of your timeline view ), the export process may hang indefinitely with a spinning "Exporting..." modal. This occurs when the plan view contains custom icons (such as for Priorities, Issue Types, or Statuses) that are hosted as attachments on a Confluence site (e.g., ...atlassian.net/wiki/download/attachments/...{}}}). *Technical Details* The export engine renders the plan into an HTML canvas. While the Confluence attachment URL appears to be same-origin, it performs a 302 redirect to a media processing domain ( api.media.atlassian.com{}}}). Browsers treat this redirected request as cross-origin. When the canvas attempts to serialize the view into a PNG file ( toDataURL{}}}), the browser triggers a } (Tainted Canvas) because the cross-origin image lacks the necessary CORS headers. The Jira Plans export tool currently does not catch this specific error, resulting in an infinite loading state in the UI. h3. Steps to Reproduce * Configure a Jira Priority or Issue Type to use a custom icon hosted as a Confluence attachment. * Create a Jira Plan that includes a column displaying this Priority or Issue Type. * Navigate to Share > Export > Export an image of your timeline view (.png) . * Click Export . h3. Expected Results The PNG file should be generated, or an error message should be displayed if an asset cannot be included. h3. Actual Results The export modal displays "Exporting X work items..." with a spinner that never resolves. The browser console shows: SecurityError: Failed to execute 'toDataURL' on 'HTMLCanvasElement': Tainted canvases may not be exported h3. Workaround * *Option 1:* Hide the column containing the custom icon (e.g., Priority or Issue Type) from the plan view before exporting. * *Option 2:* Change the custom icon to a built-in Jira icon or an image hosted on a service that supports CORS headers. * *Option 3:* Use the browser's native *Print > Save as PDF* function to capture a visual of the timeline.

title: Jira Cloud List view URL redirects to a "Not Found" (404) error in projects with multiple boards when the URL lacks a Board ID.
description: h3. Issue Summary Jira Cloud List view URL redirects to a "Not Found" (404) error in projects with multiple boards when the URL lacks a Board ID. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Create a Company-Managed Project with at least two boards (e.g., Board A and Board B). # On Board A , create a new List view via the "+" icon in the sidebar and select "Add to navigation." # Copy the resulting URL (which typically looks like /jira/software/c/projects/KEY/list/VIEW_ID{}}}). Note that this URL does not contain a boardId{}}}. # As a user whose "last viewed board" or default board is Board B , attempt to open the copied URL. h3. Expected Results Jira should resolve the List view navigation item regardless of which board the user was last viewing and display the list of issues. h3. Actual Results Jira attempts to resolve the view against the user's current/default board ( Board B ). Since the navigation item was created on Board A , the application fails to find it and redirects the user to: } h3. Workaround There are two ways to bypass this behavior: # Explicit URL : Manually construct the URL to include the specific Board ID where the view was created: } # Update Last Used Board : Navigate to the board that "owns" the List view first. This updates the session's "last used board" and ensures the original URL resolves correctly for the remainder of the session.

title: Issue View: Status message not defined programmatically
description:
h3. Issue Summary Upon activating the "Save" button, no visual confirmation or screen reader announcement is provided to confirm that the comment was saved. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Open the Jira service management home page. # Navigate to the Sidebar, expand "Spaces", and open any space. # Navigate and activate the "Queue" button from the Sidebar. # Navigate and open any work item from the data table. # Navigate to the "Add internal note" or "Reply to customer" button. # Navigate to the "Comment" field and enter any text. # Using a screen reader, navigate to "Save" button and activate it. # Observe that there is no visual confirmation or screen reader announcement confirming that the comment was saved. h3. Screen Recording [^Screen Recording 2026-10-22 at 5.23.44 PM.mov] h3. Actual Results When users activate the "Save" button after entering a value in the "Comment" input field, no visual confirmation or screen reader announcement is provided to indicate that the comment has been successfully added to the ticket. As a result, screen reader users are not informed that the comment was successfully added. h3. Expected Results When the "Save" button is activated and the comment is successfully added, provide a visible status message on the page and ensure that it is announced by screen readers without shifting focus. Implement an ARIA live region to announce the dynamic update to screen reader users. This can be achieved by using role="status" or aria-live="polite" with aria-atomic="true" on the container that displays the status message. Ensure that the live region is present in the page source by default so that dynamically inserted messages are announced reliably. For more information on implementing the live regions, visit [https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/ARIA_Live_Regions] *Note:* This code example is intended only as a general illustration of how to address the violation and should not be considered a complete or production-ready solution. If you have any questions, please attach this ticket to a #help-accessibility request. *Code Snippet:*
Comment saved successfully
h3. Workaround Currently there is no known workaround for this behavior. A workaround will be added here when available h3.
