title: Connect-to-Forge migrated app workflow rules (e.g., JMWE) not displayed in app extension discovery pages
description: h3. Issue Summary } returns Connect rule keys instead of Forge keys for Connect-to-Forge migrated apps.(JMWE) h3. Steps to Reproduce # NA h3. Expected Results The } endpoint translates and returns the migrated Forge rule keys ( migratedExtensions{}}}), allowing app management pages to discover and display all configured workflow rules. h3. Actual Results The } endpoint returns the stored legacy Connect rule keys. Because of this, centralized app management screens cannot identify the rules and display an empty list / 0 rules found. h3. Workaround Open the affected workflow in the native Jira Workflow Editor, make an update/edit, and publish the workflow draft. This re-saves the workflow rules with the updated format so they appear in the app's discovery page.

title: Adding a JPD user who is a Jira Guest user to a JPD space has a 500 failure.
description: h3. Issue Summary Adding a JPD user who is a Jira Guest user to a JPD space has a 500 failure. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Take a test user with no access to Jira or JPD at [admin.atlassian.com|http://admin.atlassian.com/] level. # Grant the user Jira guest permissions first. (this is important, I was only able to replicate in this order. Then wait a few min, refresh etc. # Grant the user JPD creator license # Navigate to a space (i tested on a private space), try to add the user. h3. Expected Results User can be added h3. Actual Results 500 Error h3. Workaround Temporarily remove the guest user access, add the user back to JPD space, this would be successful, then grant the user Jira guest access again.

title: Backlog inline status dropdown is obscured/hidden behind the Issue Preview Panel on smaller viewports
description: h3. Issue Summary In Jira Software Cloud, when the *Issue Preview Panel* (Side Panel) is open on the Backlog view, the inline status transition dropdown for backlog rows is rendered behind the preview panel. This occurs when the browser window width or screen size is small enough that the dropdown overlaps with the panel boundary. h3. Steps to Reproduce * Navigate to a Jira Software Backlog (Company-managed project). * Click on any issue card to open it in the *Issue Preview Panel* on the right. * Ensure the browser window is narrow enough (or use a laptop screen) so that the backlog rows are adjacent to the preview panel. * Click the *Status lozenge* on a different issue row within the backlog list to open the transition dropdown. * Observe the dropdown menu.   h3. Expected Results The status transition dropdown should render on top of all other UI elements (highest z-index) so that all transition options are visible. h3. Actual Results The dropdown menu is clipped or completely hidden behind the Issue Preview Panel, making it impossible to select certain transitions. !2026-10-20_11-23-09.png|thumbnail!   h3. Workaround * Use the status transition lozenge located *inside* the Issue Preview Panel for the selected issue. * Close the Issue Preview Panel before attempting to transition issues directly from the backlog list rows. *Environment Notes* * Reproduced on : Firefox 157, Chrome 130, and Edge. * Viewport : Occurs at 100% zoom on standard laptop screens or narrowed browser windows. * Surface : } with viewMode: PREVIEW_PANEL{}}}.

title: Site Optimizer fails to delete JSM portal-only customers from space roles and cannot clear orphaned "Deleted roles"
description: h3. Issue Summary Site Optimizer fails to delete JSM portal-only customer accounts from space roles and cannot remove orphaned "Deleted roles". h3. Steps to Reproduce # Step 1 Navigate to Settings > System > Site Optimizer (or Site Cleaner). # Step 2 Scan space/project roles on a Jira Service Management space containing: Portal-only customer accounts (qm:... UUIDs) assigned under the Service Desk Customers role. Role assignments referencing deleted project roles (e.g., Deleted roles (2)). Select the affected space role entries and attempt to delete/clean them up. Refresh or re-run the Site Optimizer scan h3. Expected Results Site Optimizer successfully deletes all selected space role entries, including portal-only customer assignments and orphaned references to deleted roles. h3. Actual Results The UI reports successful deletion, but the backend silently fails/skips removing portal-only customer accounts because standard Jira role-actor deletion APIs cannot remove accounts managed through JSM's customer access layer. Orphaned records referencing deleted roles also remain stuck in the database, and subsequent scans continue to show the same entries. The below exception is thrown in the xxxxxxx.log file: ... h3. Workaround Currently there is no known workaround for this behavior. A workaround will be added here when available
comment: Engineer Note: In our environment, Site Optimizer reported successful removal of the identified space role permissions; however, the entries remained present after the operation completed. This creates a misleading experience for administrators because the tool indicates that remediation has been successful when the underlying role assignments have not actually been removed. From an administrator perspective, Site Optimizer should either: * Successfully remove the identified entries, or * Clearly identify which records cannot be removed and explain why, rather than reporting a successful clean-up. The issue is particularly confusing because the UI only exposes counts and does not provide sufficient information for administrators to understand which role assignments are affected or which entries are unsupported by the deletion process. The remaining "Deleted roles" entries are also problematic because there is currently no customer-visible mechanism to resolve them, leaving Site Optimizer permanently reporting issues that administrators are unable to remediate.

title: Uploading email addresses with trailing whitespace in Account merges causes user mappings to be skipped
description: h3. Issue Summary Account merges preserves trailing whitespace in email addresses uploaded in a CSV file. This can prevent an address from matching an existing user and cause the user mapping to be skipped instead of processed. Account merges should trim leading and trailing whitespace from email addresses before looking up users. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Open Account merges in Atlassian Administration and select a Jira site. # Prepare a CSV with the columns old_email and new_email, using the email addresses of two existing users. # Add a trailing space after the destination email address in the new_email column. # Upload the CSV and run the merge. # Download the per-user results report and check the affected mapping. h3. Expected Results Account merges trims leading and trailing whitespace from both email columns before looking up users. The mapping is processed as if the email addresses had been entered without surrounding whitespace. h3. Actual Results The trailing whitespace is preserved rather than trimmed. If the address does not resolve to a user, the mapping is skipped and the requested data transfer does not occur. When the email lookup returns no matching user, the per-user results report records: status: SKIPPED error_message: No Users found with old_email or new_email h3. Workaround Remove leading and trailing whitespace from email addresses in both CSV columns before uploading the file. Review the per-user results report after the merge to verify that the mappings were processed.

title: Quick Filter URL parameter visually selected but not functionally applied on page load
description: h3. Issue Summary When navigating to a Jira Software board using a direct URL containing a } parameter, the UI correctly highlights the filter button as active (blue), but the issue list remains unfiltered. The board displays all issues until the user manually toggles the filter off and back on, which forces a functional refresh of the JQL h3. Steps to Reproduce # Identify a valid Quick Filter ID for a board (e.g., 12069{}}}). # Access the board directly via a URL with the parameter: } # *Observed Behavior:* The page loads and the "Antwerpen" filter button is visually active. However, the issues displayed on the board are *not* filtered by the Quick Filter's JQL. # *Expected Behavior:* The board should load with the Quick Filter JQL applied to the issue results immediately. # *Manual Workaround:* Click the active filter button to disable it, then click it again. The board then correctly filters the issues. h3. Expected Results When a user accesses a Jira board via a URL containing a } parameter (e.g., ?quickFilter=12069{}}}), the board should initialize with the corresponding JQL filter applied. The issue list should only display work items that match the Quick Filter criteria immediately upon page load. h3. Actual Results The board UI correctly highlights the Quick Filter button as active (blue), but the functional JQL is not executed. The board displays the full, unfiltered list of issues. The filter only becomes functionally active after the user manually toggles the button off and back on. h3. Workaround The most reliable workaround is to manually click the visually "active" Quick Filter button to disable it, and then click it again to enable it. This manual interaction forces the board to re-evaluate the JQL and correctly refresh the issue list.
comment:
Engineer Note: Another affected customer here. This issue is causing operational problems for our team because they don’t realise that the queue opened from a direct link hasn’t been filtered correctly. As a result, they are picking up issues that don’t belong to the queue they intended to work from. Because the filter still appears to be selected, there’s no obvious indication that the displayed results are incorrect.

title: Due Date field on Issue Cards does not update immediately on the Board after modification in the Issue Modal (Company-managed projects)
description: h3. Issue Summary In Company-managed projects, when a user updates the *Due Date* field via the Issue Modal (opened from a Board), the change is not reflected on the Issue Card displayed on the board until the page is manually refreshed. _P.S.: This issue will also occur, even if you open the Board from a bookmark or recognised URL. It's a board level bug so it will occur, irrespective of how the Board is loaded in the browser._ h3. Steps to Reproduce * Navigate to a Board of a Company-managed project. * Click on an Issue Card to open the *Issue Modal* (overlay). * Locate the *Due Date* field and change its value to a different date. * Close the Issue Modal to return to the Board view. * Observe the Due Date value displayed on the Issue Card. h3. Expected Results The Due Date field on the Issue Card should update dynamically to reflect the new value immediately after the modal is closed. h3. Actual Results The Issue Card continues to display the old Due Date value. A manual browser refresh is required to see the updated information. h3. Workaround Users will have to manually reload the Board in the browser to see the updated Due Date field value on the Issue card. Or they will have to wait 5-7 seconds for the value to get refreshed.

title: Epic timeline bar is not displayed on the Timeline when the epic and its child work items have only a Due date set
description: h3. Issue Summary In the Timeline view of a Jira Software space, an epic's bar disappears completely when: * the epic has only a *Due date* (no Start date ), and * at least one of its child work items also has only a *Due date* (no Start date ). When the epic has only a Due date and its child work items have no dates, a short dashed (partial-date) bar appears on the epic's due date, as expected. Once a child work item is given a due date, the epic's bar is no longer displayed at all. This makes it hard to see when epics are planned. The epic looks as if it has no dates on the Timeline, even though a due date is set. h3. Steps to Reproduce # In Jira Cloud, open a Jira Software space and go to Timeline . Make sure no filters are applied to the Timeline view. # Create an epic and set only its Due date . Leave *Start date* empty. # Check the epic's row on the Timeline. A short dashed bar is shown on the due date. This is expected. # Create a child work item (e.g. a Task) under the epic. Set only its *Due date* and leave *Start date* empty. # Check the epic's row on the Timeline again. h3. Expected Results The epic should still show a bar on the Timeline, like the short dashed partial-date bar in step 3. Neither the epic nor its child work items have a start date, so the rolled-up date range is still a partial date and should be shown as a partial-date bar. h3. Actual Results Nothing is shown for the epic on the Timeline. The dashed partial-date bar from step 3 disappears once the child work item has a Due date. For reference, these combinations work as expected:   ||Epic dates||Child work item dates||Result on Timeline|| |Due date only|None|Short dashed bar on the epic's due date (expected)| |Due date only|Due date only|*No bar shown for the epic (bug)*| |Start date and Due date|Any|Bar shown for the epic's date range (expected)| h3. Workaround Currently there is no known workaround for this behavior. A workaround will be added here when available

title: Timeline filter options are limited to the scope of work items in the backlog
description: h3. Issue Summary When applying a filter in the Timeline view of a Jira space, the available filter options (e.g., Status, Labels) are populated based only on the values present in work items currently on the project's board backlog, not on all issues visible in the Timeline view. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Open a Jira project and navigate to the *Timeline* view. # Ensure there are issues visible in the Timeline that are *not* currently present in the board's backlog (e.g., epics). # Click on the *Filter* option in the Timeline view (e.g., filter by Status or Labels). # Observe the available filter values in the dropdown. *(i) Inspecting the payload of the request made by the browser when clicking to show the filter options, we see the following:* }, "searchString": "" } Note that the } is explicitly set to } with a specific boardId{}}}. This confirms the filter values are being fetched exclusively from the board's backlog context, rather than from the full set of issues displayed in the Timeline view. ## Notice that filter values tied to issues visible in the Timeline but absent from the backlog are not listed as options. h3. Expected Results The filter dropdown in the Timeline view should display all values relevant to the issues visible in the Timeline, regardless of whether those issues are present in the board's backlog. Alternatively, it should allow users to manually type and apply custom filter values not listed in the dropdown. h3. Actual Results The filter options shown in the Timeline view are limited to values sourced from issues in the *board's backlog* only. Issues visible in the Timeline that are not in the backlog are not represented in the filter options, making it impossible to filter by values exclusive to those issues using the dropdown. h3. Workaround Set up a *Quick Filter* on the board with the desired filter criteria. Quick Filters can be configured manually with custom JQL and are not subject to the same backlog-scoped value loading behavior, allowing users to filter Timeline content more broadly.

title: Inconsistent validation behavior: Global Create dialog fails to surface required field errors on non-active tabs, unlike Project List view.
description: *Overview:* There is a significant inconsistency in how Jira Cloud handles mandatory field validation across different "Create Issue" experiences for Modern issue view experience. When a required field is located on a non-active tab (e.g., Tab 2) while the user is viewing the primary tab (Tab 1), the Global Create dialog fails to provide any visual feedback or error message upon submission. However, the Project List view correctly identifies and surfaces the error. *Steps to Reproduce:* # Configure an Issue Type Screen Scheme where the *Create Screen* has multiple tabs (e.g., "General" and "Details"). # Set a field located on the second tab ("Details") as *Required* in the Field Configuration. # *Scenario A (Global Create):* Click the global *Create* button. Fill in all required fields on the first tab. Leave the required field on the second tab empty. Click Create . # *Scenario B (List View):* Go to a Project -> List View . Click *+ Create* at the bottom of the list. Fill in the first tab and leave the second tab's required field empty. Click Create . *Expected Results:* In both scenarios, the UI should clearly indicate that a required field on another tab is missing (e.g., a red badge on the tab header or an error message stating "Field X is required"). *Actual Results:* * *Global Create Dialog:* The dialog does nothing or "fails silently." The user remains on Tab 1 with no error message, and the issue is not created. There is no visual cue that Tab 2 contains the blocker unless the user navigates to the Tab 2. * *Project List View:* Correctly surfaces the error message and indicates the validation failure even though the field is on a different tab. *Impact:* This inconsistency causes significant user confusion and friction. Users perceive the Global Create dialog as "broken" because it provides no feedback, leading to multiple support tickets and abandoned issue creation attempts. *Workaround:* Move all required fields to the first/primary tab of the screen configuration. Loom recording: https://www.loom.com/share/5f74efa43f0a44478e228a7c53925940
comment:
Engineer Note: Urgent fix needed! User experience is impaired!

title: Jira Expressions evaluating issue.parent, checks the saved database value instead of the updated Parent selected on the new Transition Screen
description: h3. Issue Summary When transitioning an issue using a transition screen where the *Parent* field is updated, workflow validators using Jira Expressions (such as custom expression validators or validators provided by *third-party apps like ScriptRunner, JWT, or JMWE)* do not evaluate the new Parent value selected on the screen. Instead, the Jira Expressions engine evaluates } against the value currently saved in the database before the transition. This causes two problematic behaviors: # *Setting a new Parent on an unparented issue:* If an issue previously had no parent, } evaluates as null, causing conditions (such as checking parent status) to fail or throw an error even though a valid parent was selected on the screen. # *Changing an existing Parent:* If an issue is being moved from a closed parent to an open parent, the validator checks the status of the previous (closed) parent and blocks the transition with an error indicating the parent is closed. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Configure a workflow transition screen that includes the *Parent* field. (New Transition Screen) # Add a Jira Expression validator to the transition checking the parent's status (e.g., issue.parent.status.category.key != "done"{}}}). (Using third-party apps ScriptRunner, JWT,... ) # Attempt to transition an issue that currently has a closed parent (or no parent), and select a valid, open Epic in the *Parent* field on the transition screen. # Submit the transition. h3. Expected Results The validator checks the newly selected Parent from the transition screen and allows the transition to proceed. h3. Actual Results The validator checks the Parent value currently saved in the database (the old parent or null), causing the validation to fail and blocking the transition. Error:  "Fill in the Parent field with an epic that is still open, or reopen the epic in question."   h3. Workaround * Update the *Parent* field directly on the issue view before initiating the workflow transition. * Alternatively, use Jira Automation rules to validate and update parent links after the transition completes, rather than using a transition screen validator.

title: Status on issue card not updating and requires page refresh
description: h3. Issue Summary When an issue is transitioned between statuses that are mapped to the same column, the status on the issue card is not updated automatically and requires a page refresh. When the issue is transitioned to a status that is mapped to a different column, the issue card is moved and the status on the card is updated as expected. h3. Steps to Reproduce * Setup a Kanban board that has two or more statuses mapped to one column * Add the "Status" field to the issue card layout * Transition an issue (via transition dropdown from the issue view) between statuses that are mapped to the same column h3. Expected Results The status on the issue card should be automatically updated, the same way it happens when the issue is moved to a different column h3. Actual Results The status on the issue card remains with the previous value until the page is refreshed h3. Workaround The issue card is updated after a page refresh
comment:
Engineer Note: This bug significantly disrupts our workflow
Engineer Note: This bug has come back and has been affecting us consistently for the last couple of months. On the Kanban board, cards frequently stay in the column of their previous status after the work item has already been transitioned. The board does not pick up the new status automatically, and a single page refresh is often not enough - it takes several refreshes before the card finally moves to the correct column. Steps to reproduce: 1. Open a Kanban board 2. Transition a work item to another status (from the board, or from the work item view) 3. Look at the board Expected Results: the card is immediately shown in the column matching its current status, with no manual refresh. Actual Results: the card remains in the old status column. Refreshing the page once frequently does not help; several refreshes are needed before the board renders the correct state. This did not happen before - the board used to update correctly. It is disruptive to daily work, so it would be good to have this reopened or tracked as a new regression.

title: Deleting an unused global work type fails with HTTP 500 "Illegal Entity Scope for Entity class (FIELD_ASSOCIATION_SCHEME)" when a team-managed project's field scheme references the work type
description: h3. Issue Summary Admins can't delete a global work type that has no work items. The delete fails with an HTTP 500 error in both the UI and the REST API ( DELETE /rest/api/3/issuetype/\ }}}): Illegal Entity Scope for Entity class (FIELD_ASSOCIATION_SCHEME). Expected entity scope 'GLOBAL' but has scope 'PROJECT' This happens when a project-scoped field association scheme, which belongs to a team-managed project, has explicit field associations to the global work type being deleted. For example, a custom field such as Story Points may be restricted to that work type. The deletion check expects every scheme that references a global work type to be global. When it finds a project-scoped scheme, it throws an unhandled exception and doesn't clean up the reference. The admin has no way to see or remove these project-scoped associations in the UI or the API, so the work type can't be deleted. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Have a team-managed project whose field association scheme has explicit associations to one or more global work types. For example, a custom field like Story Points restricted to those global work types. # Make sure the global work types have no work items. The delete page shows "There are currently no matching work items". # Go to *Settings > Work items > Work types* and try to delete one of those global work types. You can also call DELETE /rest/api/3/issuetype/\ }}}. h3. Expected Results The unused global work type is deleted. Any field associations that reference it in project-scoped schemes are removed or ignored, or the admin sees a clear message saying which project or configuration is blocking the deletion. h3. Actual Results The deletion fails with HTTP 500. The UI shows a generic error, and the REST API returns:    Illegal Entity Scope for Entity class (FIELD_ASSOCIATION_SCHEME). Expected entity scope 'GLOBAL' but has scope 'PROJECT' The work type stays on the site. The error doesn't say which project or scheme is causing it. *Notes* * It's not yet clear how a team-managed project's field scheme ends up with associations to global work types. Root cause is under investigation. * In a related symptom, the delete page for an affected work type can show "0 active and 0 archived work items" but also "used by 1 work item in archived projects", without naming a project or work item. h3. Workaround None available to admins. Contact [Atlassian Support|https://support.atlassian.com/contact/] to have the stale field associations removed so the work type can be deleted.

title: Summary tab board filter breaks if more than one parameter is added to the filter
description: h3. Issue Summary Summary tab board filter breaks if more than one parameter is added to the filter h3. Steps to Reproduce # Navigate to a Kanban Board # Select Summary tab. # Select Filter  # Add one filter -> Works fine # Add a second filter -> Activity tab breaks with "Something went wrong error" # Loom video with replication: https://www.loom.com/share/a0d4710351504508b1c7785be4f81dae h3. title: Header: Bookmark links do not work
description:
h3. Issue Summary The "Skip to: Top Bar," "Main Content," "Sidebar," and "Space navigation" links are not keyboard-operable. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Open the Jira Cloud homepage. # Navigate to the header section and press Shift+Tab to access the skip links. # Use the Tab key to sequentially navigate through the "Top Bar," "Main Content," "Sidebar," and "Space Navigation" links. # Try to activate each link using the Enter key. # Observe that the focus remains on the activated link. h3. Screenshot !Screenshot 2026-06-09 at 1.18.15 PM.png|width=254,height=135! h3. Screen Recording [https://www.loom.com/share/da714223f8444e5c9430e33ad917d1da] h3.   ...

If you have any questions, please attach this ticket to a #help-accessibility request. h3. Workaround Currently there is no known workaround for this behavior. title: When Jira Cloud is connected to Jira Data Center using an Application Tunnel (with OAuth Application Links), remote issue link icons (Issue Type and Priority) fail to render in the Jira Cloud issue view and appear as broken image placeholders.
description: h3. Issue Summary Remote link icons (issue type and priority) are not rendered and appear as broken images when connected to Jira Data Center via Application Tunnel h3. Steps to Reproduce # Connect a Jira Cloud instance to a Jira Data Center instance using an *Application Tunnel* (OAuth Application Link). # Create a remote issue link on a Jira Cloud issue pointing to an issue in the connected Jira Data Center instance. # Open the Jira Cloud issue in the web browser and view the linked items section. h3. Expected Results The remote link renders cleanly with the remote Jira Data Center issue key, summary, status, priority icon, and issue type icon. h3. Actual Results * The issue key, summary, and status load successfully, but the *Issue Type* and *Priority* icons fail to render and appear as broken images. * Inspecting the GraphQL response for } shows } and } returning the internal tunnel RPC host ( http://<tunnel-id>.self-hosted.atlassian.com/...{}}}) instead of the public displayUrl{}}}. * The browser cannot access this internal endpoint directly, resulting in the image requests failing. The below exception is thrown in the browser developer tools / network console:       } The below exception is thrown in the xxxxxxx.log file: ... h3. Workaround Currently there is no known workaround for this behavior. A workaround will be added here when available
comment:
Engineer Note: *Engineering diagnosis* *Root cause* When Jira Cloud is connected to a Data Center instance via an Application Tunnel, the remote issue link's icon URLs (issue type and priority) are returned using the Application Link's internal RPC host instead of its public display host. The browser cannot reach that internal host, so the icon requests time out ( ERR_CONNECTION_TIMED_OUT{}}}) and the icons render as broken images. This is not a Data Center problem as it returns the icon URLs correctly against its display/base URL. The issue is that the Cloud read path does not rewrite the icon host from the RPC URL to the display URL before returning it to the browser. *Why only icons break* The key, summary, and status fields contain no host-specific URLs, so they display correctly. Only the icon/avatar fields embed the remote host, so only those are affected. *Proposed fix* Rewrite the remote link icon URLs from the RPC host to the display host on the standard remote-link read path, consistent with how other remote-link surfaces already handle this. This restores browser-accessible icon URLs and resolves the broken images.
Engineer Note: Fix PR is merged and rolled out at 100% - https://switcheroo.atlassian.com/ui/gates/f7db93fb-dd76-475e-8191-a1d2e0275e2c/key/jracloud-99489-remote-link-icon-display-url

title: Issue View: Inappropriate label for button
description: h3. Issue Summary The “4 minutes ago” button lacks a descriptive accessible name that indicates its action. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Open the Jira Cloud home page. # Navigate to the Sidebar, expand "Spaces", and open any space. # Navigate to the "List" link, activate it, and open any work item from the data table. # Navigate to the "Add a comment" button and activate it. # Navigate and activate the "Save" button. # Using a screen reader, navigate to the "4 minutes ago" button. # Press "Enter" or "Space "to activate the button. # Observe that the newly displayed date and time is not communicated to the screen reader. h3. Screen Recording [https://www.loom.com/share/7db288a413594904806720f13e32eabd] h3. Actual Results The “4 minutes ago” button, which currently displays a relative time such as “4 minutes ago,” does not convey its purpose to screen reader users when it receives focus or is activated. When activated, the button changes the displayed value to the absolute date and time (“September 28, 2026 at 3:42 PM”). However, assistive technology users are not informed about what activating the control will do or that the time representation has changed. Screen reader users hear only the time string without context indicating that it is an interactive control that toggles between relative and absolute time representations. Without a descriptive accessible name or an appropriate announcement, users cannot understand what the control does or anticipate the result of activating it. h3. Expected Results The control should have a descriptive, accessible name that clearly communicates its purpose and behavior to screen reader users. Apply the following changes: * Default state: The button should have an accessible name that clearly communicates the action to display the date and time, for example: 4 minutes ago - Show date and time. * Activated state: The button should have an accessible name that clearly communicates the action to collapse the date and time and return to the relative-time format, for example: September 28, 2026 at 3:42 PM - Hide date and time. * Visually hidden instructions: The phrases “Show date and time” and “Hide date and time” should be visually hidden using the dedicated screen-reader utility class sr-only, so the existing visual presentation remains unchanged. *Note:* This code example is intended only as a general illustration of how to address the violation and should not be considered a complete or production-ready solution. If you have any questions, please attach this ticket to a #help-accessibility request. *Note:* Please consult the Content Design team and incorporate their guidance on the exact accessible labels before implementing the change. *Code Snippet:* 4 minutes ago - Show date and time (...) September 28, 2026 at 3:42 PM - Hide date and time .sr-only h3. Workaround Currently there is no known workaround for this behavior. A workaround will be added here when availableEnvironment h3. Environment MacBook Pro (16-inch, 2023) macOs - Sequoia 15.7.9 Chrome - Version 154.0.8037.58 (Official Build) (arm64) Safari- Version 27.0 (20625.1.29.18.28) JAWS- Version 2026 NVDA- Version 2026.1 Voiceover - Version Latest

title: Issue View: Focus moves inappropriately
description: h3. Issue Summary Focus moves inappropriately after activating "Assign to me" and "Delete" button. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Open the Jira Cloud home page. # Navigate to the Sidebar, expand "Spaces", and open any space. # Navigate to the "List" link, activate it, and open any work item from the data table. # Navigate to the "Details" button in the main section and activate it. # Using a screen reader and keyboard, navigate to and activate the mentioned buttons. # Observe that the focus moves inappropriately. h3. Screen Recording [^Screen Recording 2026-09-30 at 3.31.12 PM.mov] h3. Actual Results When users activate the "Assign to me" button from the "Details" section or the "Delete" button from the "More actions" menu within the comment section, keyboard focus unexpectedly moves to the top of the page instead of remaining within the current focus sequence. As a result, keyboard-only and screen reader users are required to navigate through previously encountered content to return to their original location and continue interacting with the page. h3. Expected Results Keyboard focus should remain within the current interaction flow and move to the appropriate control or next logical interactive element after activation. Apply the following changes: * Retain the keyboard focus on the "Assignee" input filed when "Assign to me" button is activated. * When "Delete" button is activated from the comment section the keyboard focus should move to "More actions" button. For more information please refer to: [https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/focus-order]. h3. Workaround Currently there is no known workaround for this behavior. A workaround will be added here when available h3. Environment MacBook Pro (16-inch, 2023) macOs - Sequoia 15.7.9 Chrome - Version 154.0.8037.58 (Official Build) (arm64) Safari- Version 27.0 (20625.1.29.18.28) JAWS- Version 2026 NVDA- Version 2026.1 Voiceover - Version Latest

title: Issue View: Status message not defined programmatically
description:
h3. Issue Summary Upon activating the "Save" button, no visual confirmation or screen reader announcement is provided to confirm that the comment was saved. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Open the Jira Cloud home page. # Navigate to the Sidebar, expand "Spaces", and open any space. # Navigate to the "List" link, activate it, and open any work item from the data table. # Navigate to the "Add a comment" button and activate it. # Navigate to the "Comment" field and enter any text. # Using a screen reader, navigate to "Save" button and activate it. # Observe that there is no visual confirmation or screen reader announcement confirming that the comment was saved. h3. Screen Recording [^Screen Recording 2026-09-30 at 3.19.24 PM.mov] h3. Actual Results When users activate the "Save" button after entering a value in the "Comment" input field, no visual confirmation or screen reader announcement is provided to indicate that the comment has been successfully added to the ticket. As a result, screen reader users are not informed that the comment was successfully added. h3. Expected Results When the "Save" button is activated and the comment is successfully added, provide a visible status message on the page and ensure that it is announced by screen readers without shifting focus. Implement an ARIA live region to announce the dynamic update to screen reader users. This can be achieved by using role="status" or aria-live="polite" with aria-atomic="true" on the container that displays the status message. Ensure that the live region is present in the page source by default so that dynamically inserted messages are announced reliably. For more information on implementing the live regions, visit [https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/ARIA_Live_Regions] *Note:* This code example is intended only as a general illustration of how to address the violation and should not be considered a complete or production-ready solution. If you have any questions, please attach this ticket to a #help-accessibility request. *Code Snippet:*
Comment saved successfully
h3. Workaround Currently there is no known workaround for this behavior. A workaround will be added here when available. h3. title: Unable to create task on a Jira board using Jira mobile app for Android
description: h3. Issue Summary There's an issue where a new task can't be created on a Jira board while using the Jira mobile app for Android h3. Steps to Reproduce # Install the Jira mobile app for Android # Be on Android OS >= OS 15 # Access your Jira board (Sprint board) # Attempt to create a new task from the board h3. Expected Results # The task should be created h3. Actual Results # The task failed to create h3. Workaround The problem is that the "Sprint" field was not available on the screen from the mobile perspective. To resolve this issue, navigate to the *Project settings > Issues > Screens* add the field "Sprint" to the screen for the specified work type.

title: Plans "More actions" (...) menu renders permanently open on load for a specific user
description: h3. Issue Summary When a specific user loads a Plan, the "..." (more actions) menu next to the Plan name is already open and cannot be dismissed. Clicking elsewhere, pressing Escape, or interacting with other UI elements does not close it. Key observations: * Affects one specific user only, other users on the same plan are unaffected * Affects one specific plan only, other plans for the same user behave normally * Persists across all browsers, devices, and after clearing cache/local storage * Refreshing the page does not resolve the issue h3. Steps to Reproduce # Log in as the affected user # Navigate to the affected Plan # Observe: "..." menu is already open on load # Click elsewhere or press Escape # Expected: Menu closes. Actual: Menu remains open h3. Expected Results Menu renders open after a page load.  h3. Actual Results The menu state should reset on page load and respond to standard dismiss interactions. h3. Workaround Duplicating the plan and deleting the original resolves the issue, however this breaks any existing external links or references to the plan.

title: Viewing empty Story Points in the Subtasks section wraps the placeholder onto multiple lines, making rows taller and the list hard to read
description: h3. Issue Summary In the Subtasks section on the work item view, empty Story Points cells show a placeholder text ("Add story points"). When the Story Points column is narrow (default width), the placeholder wraps onto multiple lines instead of being truncated: * English UI: "Add story points" wraps over 3 lines * Japanese UI: "ストーリーポイントを追加してください" wraps over 7 lines As a result, the rows become much taller and the Subtasks list is hard to read. The column header in the same table is truncated with an ellipsis ("Story..." / "Stor..."), but the placeholder in the cell wraps. Customers report that this makes it difficult to review tasks and subtasks in the Subtasks section, and it is affecting their work. They have also found the workarounds below not practical for their use. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Open a work item that has subtasks with no Story Points value. # Show the Story Points column in the Subtasks section (keep the default column width). # Check the placeholder text in the empty Story Points cells. # Switch the Jira language to Japanese to see a more severe result. h3. Expected Results The placeholder does not affect the row height. If it does not fit the column width, it is shown on a single line and truncated with an ellipsis, like the column header. h3. Actual Results The placeholder wraps vertically within the Story Points column. The rows become much taller, and the Subtasks list is hard to read, especially in the Japanese UI. !subtasks-en.png|width=594,height=100! !subtasks-jp.png|width=578,height=139! h3. Workaround * Widen the Story Points column by dragging the column border. This keeps the placeholder on a single line. However, in the Japanese UI the column needs roughly a quarter of the table width, which reduces the space for the Summary column. * Remove the Story Points column from the Subtasks section via "Configure columns". However, existing Story Points values are also hidden from the list. Neither workaround works when users need both readable summaries and Story Points in the Subtasks section.

Steps to Reproduce # Open the Jira List view. # Enable issue grouping by Sprint . # Use a search that returns issues across multiple sprints. # Ensure that the total result set contains more than 101 issues. # Compare the grouped issue counts with the total number of issues returned by the same search without grouping. h3. Expected Results All issues matching the search criteria should be fetched and assigned to their respective sprint groups. Grouping should not reduce or alter the result set. h3. Workaround We need to tweak the JQL Filter by Specific Sprint to display the items and make sure the count is not higher

title: "Epic" and Level 1 work item types are missing from the "Type" filter dropdown in the Backlog view of Company-Managed projects
description: h3. Issue Summary The "Type" filter dropdown in the Backlog view of Company-Managed projects/boards does not list "Epic" or other custom work item types configured at Level 1 (Epic level) of the issue hierarchy. As a result, users can't filter the backlog list by Level 1 work item types using the native Type filter dropdown, even when those types are explicitly included in the board filter JQL and rendered as cards in the backlog list. Work item types above Level 1 in the hierarchy (e.g., Initiative, Theme, or other parent levels above Epic), as well as standard Level 0 types (such as Story, Bug, Task), are not affected and appear as expected. In addition, the "Type" filter dropdown in the Active Kanban Board view continues to display and filter by "Epic" and other Level 1 types normally. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Open a Company-Managed Jira Software space with a Kanban board where the Backlog is enabled and the board filter includes Epics (or other Level 1 hierarchy types). # Ensure there are Epics / Level 1 work items present in the Backlog. # Navigate to the Backlog view . # Click on the *Type* filter dropdown in the filter bar at the top of the backlog. # Attempt to select *Epic* (or another Level 1 work item type). h3. Expected Results The "Epic" work item type (and any other Level 1 hierarchy types) is available in the "Type" filter dropdown in the Backlog view, allowing users to filter the backlog by those types. h3. Actual Results The "Epic" work item type (and other Level 1 hierarchy types) is omitted from the "Type" filter dropdown in the Backlog view. Work item types above Level 1 in the hierarchy remain unaffected and display correctly. h3. Workaround There are two available workarounds to filter the backlog by Epics or Level 1 work items: * *Option 1: Create a Quick Filter (Recommended)* # Go to *Board settings* > Quick Filters . # Add a new quick filter with the query: } (or issuetype = "<WORK_ITEM_TYPE>"{}}}). # Use the newly created quick filter button directly on the Backlog view. * *Option 2: Manually append the URL query parameter* # Append * }* to the Backlog URL (e.g., ?issueType=10000{}}}).

title: Rovo MCP Server silently drops content on Markdown writes (invalid ADF blocks removed, write returns success) — Jira comments, descriptions & environment fields
description: h3. Issue Summary When writing Jira content (comments, descriptions, and environment fields) through the Rovo MCP Server using contentFormat: "markdown"{}}}, the Markdown-to-ADF conversion silently drops any block it cannot map to a valid ADF structure instead of failing the write. The write still returns a successful (HTTP 200) response, so content is lost with no error, warning, or truncation notice. This has been confirmed to affect both the v1 and v2 MCP servers when using markdown. *Root cause:* the Markdown-to-ADF conversion drops any block it cannot map to a valid ADF structure rather than rejecting the request. Confirmed cases: * A blockquote containing a heading, a nested blockquote, a table, or a horizontal rule -> the entire blockquote is dropped . * A list item containing a heading, a blockquote, a table, or a horizontal rule -> that list item is dropped, including its own text . * Bold styling that spans an inline code span -> the bold ends at the code span (no text is lost). This behavior applies to comments, descriptions, and environment fields on both the v1 and v2 servers. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Connect a client to the Rovo MCP Server (reproduces on both v1 and v2). # Call a write tool such as } or } with contentFormat: "markdown"{}}}. # Include a markdown block that cannot be mapped to valid ADF, for example a blockquote containing a heading: REPRO START. > # Heading inside a blockquote > Some body text inside the blockquote under the heading. > ## A second heading line inside the same blockquote REPRO END. # Confirm the write returns a successful response (HTTP 200 / a comment or issue id is returned). # Read the stored content back as ADF and compare it against what was sent. h3. Expected Results The write should either preserve the content by converting the invalid structure into a valid one (for example, converting headings inside blockquotes into standard paragraphs), or reject the call with an explicit client error (HTTP 400), matching the behavior of the direct ADF path. It should not silently discard content while reporting success. h3. Actual Results The offending block is silently removed and the write returns a successful (HTTP 200) response. For a blockquote containing a heading, the entire blockquote (heading and all body text) is removed; for a list item containing an invalid nested block, the whole list item and its text are removed. No error, warning, or truncation notice is returned, so the loss is only detectable by reading the stored content back as ADF and comparing it to what was sent. h3. Workaround Move to the v2 server ( [https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp]{}}}) and send } instead of markdown on } and editJiraIssue{}}}. The HTML path converts faithfully and hands any invalid nesting to Jira, which rejects it with an HTTP 400 error instead of silently dropping it. Reads with } are lossless as well, so read-edit-write flows work. Note: markdown on the v2 server has the same problem, so the workaround is specifically v2 with HTML. If you need to stay on the v1 server, } is the fallback — Jira validates the ADF and returns an HTTP 400 for these structures rather than dropping them. Otherwise, avoid the constructs listed above.
comment: Engineer Note: Hi everyone, This is James from the Jira MCP team. This bug is now fixed. Markdown writes to Jira (comments, descriptions, environment fields) that contain a heading, table, horizontal rule, or nested blockquote inside a blockquote or list item now return a clear error naming the unsupported structure and its line, instead of silently dropping the block and reporting success. This applies to both the v1 and v2 servers. The fix is live on all sites, so the workarounds in the description are no longer needed. I've confirmed the behaviour and will mark this as fixed. Thanks, James

title: USER_MERGE workflow fails for users with a very large number of linked issues (~210k rows)
description: h3. Issue Summary The Jira user merge workflow times out or fails when the input includes a user who has a very large number of issue references (assignee, reporter, creator, or user picker fields). h3. title: Jql/match API does not evaluate version comparison operators (>, >=, <, <=) for fixVersion and affectedVersion
description: h3. Issue Summary The POST /rest/api/3/jql/match endpoint does not evaluate the JQL comparison operators (>, >=, <, <=) against the fixVersion and affectedVersion fields. It silently returns an empty matchedIssues array, together with an empty errors array, instead of matching the work item. The same JQL, run against the same work item, as the same user, returns the work item correctly via POST /rest/api/3/search/jql, and returns it correctly in Jira's own work item search. Equality and set operators are not affected. Both fixVersion = "Version 3" and fixVersion IN (...) match correctly through jql/match. Only the comparison operators fail. This narrows the defect to the evaluation of the project's configured version sequence within the match path, rather than to field or value resolution in general. The JQL fields reference ([https://support.atlassian.com/jira-software-cloud/docs/jql-fields/]) documents >, >=, < and <= as supported operators for both fixVersion and affectedVersion, and states that these comparison operators use the version order configured by the space administrator rather than a numeric or alphabetic order. There is no documented restriction limiting which JQL clauses jql/match supports, so the current behaviour is undocumented as well as inconsistent. h3. Steps to Reproduce # In a Jira Cloud project, create three versions, ordered as follows in the project's version sequence: Version 1, then Version 2, then Version 3. # Create one work item, TEST-1, and set its Fix Version to Version 3. # Note the numeric id of TEST-1, referred to below as issueId. # Call the search endpoint with a comparison clause: POST /rest/api/3/search/jql Confirm that TEST-1 is returned.       5. Call the match endpoint with the same JQL and that work item id:   POST /rest/api/3/jql/match        6. Repeat step 5 substituting >=, < and <=, and substituting affectedVersion for fixVersion. h3. Expected Results jql/match reports the work item as matching, consistent with search/jql and with Jira's work item search: ] } h3. Actual Results jql/match reports no match, and reports no error: ] } Confirmed by the reporter to occur with all four comparison operators (>, >=, <, <=) and with both fixVersion and affectedVersion. Not affected, and confirmed working through the same endpoint: fixVersion = "Version 3" and fixVersion IN (...). The empty errors array is the most damaging part of this behaviour. The API accepts the query and reports a definite negative result rather than rejecting the clause, so a calling application has no signal that distinguishes an unsupported clause from a genuine non-match. The failure is silent and indistinguishable from correct operation. h3. Workaround Currently there is no known workaround for this behavior. A workaround will be added here when available
comment: Engineer Note: Fix is deployed and rolled out for all tenants

title: Confluence Cloud API rate limiting incorrectly counts some API usage, causing premature HTTP 429 responses
description: h4. *Problem Description* Some Marketplace apps and API integrations using Confluence Cloud may get premature HTTP 429 Too Many Requests responses ( ratelimit-reason: conf-tenant-based){}}} during normal use, even when their overall traffic is within expected limits. Once a site reaches its rate limit, later Confluence REST API calls are throttled. Dependent apps may then fail to load data or show errors until the rate-limit window resets. h4. *Steps to Reproduce* _Note: This issue cannot be reproduced on production environments once the configuration fix has been deployed._  1.  Install and configure a Marketplace app or custom API integration that makes standard Confluence Cloud REST API calls (for example, read requests that return multiple pages or spaces).  2.  Run normal daily traffic across users.  3.  Some API usage is incorrectly counted against the site's rate-limit allowance.  4.  The site reaches its rate limit earlier than expected, and Confluence Cloud returns: HTTP 429 Too Many Requests ratelimit-reason: conf-tenant-based h4. *Expected Results* API requests are tracked accurately against tenant point quotas based on their actual resource consumption, allowing normal traffic to operate without premature throttling. h4. *Actual Results* Certain API requests are erroneously counted against the tenant's rate-limit allowance, triggering rate limiting well before actual usage warrants it. h4. *Workaround* During active investigation, Atlassian Engineering applied manual rate-limit exemptions to affected cloud instances to prevent throttling and maintain service stability.
comment: Engineer Note: The bug was fixed via the PR: [https://bitbucket.org/atlassian/confluence/pull-requests/75907] We have monitored and seen that the impact to the customer is now resolved.   The original [https://atlassiansupport.atlassian.net/browse/CES-194464] ticket has also been closed.   Hence marking the bugfix as resolved.   The other linked ECO ticket [https://ecosystem.atlassian.net/browse/ECOHELP-164319] needs support in general about global rate limiting and further questions are not associated to this bug.   Hence resolving it.

title: Bulk Workflows API omits parameters.disabled for migrated Connect→Forge rules
description: h3. Issue Summary When a Forge app migrates its workflow modules from Connect to Forge (keeping the same module keys), Jira’s bulk Workflows API ( POST /rest/api/3/workflows{}}}) returns the existing rule instances as  } rules but omits the  } field from the response — even though the flag is still stored and honoured internally. As a result, any subsequent workflow save via  } — whether triggered by the app, the workflow editor, or an admin publishing the workflow — writes back the rules without the  } flag, permanently re-activating every rule that was previously disabled. Affected customers experience validators blocking transitions and conditions hiding transition buttons, with no visible indication of the cause. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Set up a workflow with Forge workflow rules (validators, conditions, post-functions) that were originally created as Connect rules and have some set to disabled ( parameters.disabled: "true"{}}}). # Migrate the app’s workflow modules from Connect to Forge, keeping the same module keys. # Call  } to read the workflow — the rules now appear as  } rules, but  } is missing from the response. _(Note: the transition still works at this point, confirming the flag is still stored.)_ # Call  } sending back exactly what step 3 returned — or simply open the workflow in the Jira workflow editor and publish it. # Observe that the previously disabled rules are now active — conditions hide transitions, validators block them. h3. Expected Results } should include  } in the response for rules that have the disabled flag set, regardless of whether they were originally registered as Connect or Forge rules. A round-trip read → write should preserve the disabled state. h3. Actual Results } omits  } when projecting Connect rule instances as  } rules. Any subsequent  } using this response re-enables all previously disabled rules. Admins cannot detect this — the app’s own UI still shows the rules as disabled, while Jira is actively enforcing them. h3. Workaround Currently there is no known workaround for this behavior. A workaround will be added here when available
comment: Engineer Note: We have finished rolling out the FG preserving the "isDisabled" parameter in the workflow APIs. The parameter should now appear for Connect rules that have been converted to Forge.

title: Issue View: Incorrect focus management for tabs
description: h3. Issue Summary Tab navigation has incorrect focus handling. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Open the Jira/JSM homepage. # Navigate to the Sidebar, expand "Spaces", and open any space. # Navigate to the "List" link, activate it, and open any work item from the data table. # Using a screen reader and keyboard, navigate to the "Default," "Test Details," or "A11y Test" tab within the tab list. # Press the Right Arrow key to navigate to the next tab. # Observe that the next tab is selected, but focus unexpectedly moves to another location on the page. h3. Screen Recording [Focus Management Issue|https://www.loom.com/share/6a0b3ca427e14a58b63918f0ed353190] h3. Actual Results When users navigate between the "Default", "Test Details", and "A11y Test" tabs and press the Right Arrow key to move to the next tab, the next tab is selected correctly; however, programmatic focus unexpectedly moves to a different location on the page instead of remaining on the newly selected tab. This results in inconsistent focus behavior and prevents keyboard and screen reader users from navigating the tab list effectively. h3. Expected Results Keyboard navigation should follow standard accessibility behavior, allowing users to move focus and navigate between tabs using appropriate keys without unexpected focus shifts. Apply the following changes: * When focus is on the tablist, pressing the Left/Right Arrow keys should move focus between  "Default", "Test Details", and "A11y Test" tabs within the same tablist. * Focus should remain within the tablist when using arrow key navigation. * Focus should only move out of the tablist when the Tab key is used. For guidance on creating an accessible tab component, refer to: [Accessible Tabs Pattern|https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tabs/]. h3. Workaround Currently there is no known workaround for this behavior. A workaround will be added here when available h3. Environment MacBook Pro (16-inch, 2021) macOS Tahoe 26.6.2 Windows 11 Chrome - 153.0.8010.48 (Official Build) (64-bit) Microsoft Edge - 153.0.4234.32 (Official build) (64-bit) Safari- Version 26.6.2 JAWS- Version 2026 NVDA- Version 2026.2 VoiceOver - Version Latest

title: JSIS JQL search for comments/description/text returns incorrect results for values stored in some ADF nodes like mentions or inlinelinks
description: h3. Issue Summary JQL search returns incorrect results when searching for values stored in some type of ADF nodes. Examples: * Team Mentions via UUID * User Mentions via UUID * URLs in some links h3. Steps to Reproduce # Mention an Atlassian Team in a Jira issue comment or description (for example, mention the team "Jira Admin Support"). # Identify the Team's UUID (for example, 74e55c45-c3fd-4fc0-8a9d-675b0872de9{}}}). # Perform an advanced JQL search using the } operator and the team's UUID string: comment ~ "team/{}}} 74e55c45-c3fd-4fc0-8a9d-675b0872de9{}}} "{}}} or description ~ "team/{}}} 74e55c45-c3fd-4fc0-8a9d-675b0872de9{}}} "{}}}. # Observe the search results. h3. Expected Results Jira should return all issues where the specified team was mentioned in the comments or description, as the UUID is a stable, unique identifier stored within the mention's metadata. h3. Actual Results The search returns "No issues found," even though the team is correctly mentioned in the issues. The search engine is currently only indexing the human-readable display name of the team, ignoring the underlying unique identifier (UUID) previously stored in the } attribute of the mention. h3. Workaround (for mentions) Users can search using the team's *Display Name* instead of the UUID. To improve accuracy and reduce false positives, use an escaped exact-phrase search:   } *Limitations of this workaround:* * *Lack of Identity Stability:* If the team is renamed, the JQL filter will break and must be updated manually. * *Precision Issues:* This search will return results for any instance where the team's name is typed as plain text, not just when the team is formally @mentioned . * *Ambiguity:* If multiple teams have similar names, the search may return results for the wrong team.
comment: Engineer Note: Hi everyone, we rolled out a fix in September for the incorrect JQL search results affecting mention identifiers and URLs in comments and descriptions. We haven’t observed any new occurrences since the rollout, so we’re closing this issue as resolved. If you continue to experience this behaviour, please contact Atlassian Support with an example so we can investigate. Thank you for your patience.

title: Script runner's validator fails to recognise updates (clearing field) following the enablement of the Modern Transition Screen Experience.
description: h3. Issue Summary Script runner's validator fails to recognise updates (clearing field) following the enablement of the Modern Transition Screen Experience. When a workflow transition is configured with a plugin (script runner) validator (e.g., "Field Required" or "Validate a field") targeting paragraph field, the validator fails to block the transition if the field is updated/cleared directly on the  Transition Screen . The validator appears to evaluate the issue's state _before_ the transition screen updates are applied, rather than validating the new values provided during the transition. *Note: This is reproducible in the New/Modern Transition Experience (this is not reproducible in the Old Transition Screen experience - [https://community.atlassian.com/t5/Jira-articles/Now-GA-try-the-new-issue-transition-experience-in-Jira/ba-p/2734436]*  h3. Steps to Reproduce # Ensure the *New Modern Transition Screen* experience is enabled for the site # Configure a workflow transition with a validator (e.g., ensure to keep the field empty if certain value is selected on another field) for the paragraph field via Script runner which has field empty validator.  # Take a work item that currently *has* a Paragraph field value. Note: The paragraph field will need to be using the legacy plain-text renderer. This isn't supported anymore, but there may be old fields around.  # Trigger the transition to open the transition screen. say Open to Done.  # On the transition screen type something into the paragraph field # Then *clear* the Paragraph field. # Click the transition button (e.g., "Update" or "Done"). h3. Expected Results The validator should identify that the Paragraph field is now empty and carry on the transition. h3. Actual Results The transition doen't occur and fails with error message even though the field value is empty. h3. Workaround Currently there is no known workaround for this behavior. A workaround will be added here when available
comment:
Engineer Note: Hey everyone,  We have identified what was going on here. When a *plain-text* paragraph field was in use and then cleared on the transition screen, the value being being submitted was an invalid ADF document. This led to an error during the processing of the expression. This was returned as a validation failure leading masking the underlying error. A fix is in flight to address this in the new transition experience by making it send a valid empty document in this situation.  Once this is done expressions like this will work in this situation.  let plainText = v => v == null ? "" : (typeof v == 'Map' ? new RichText(v).plainText : "" + v); plainText(issue.customfield_XXXXXX).trim() == "" If you are interested there is also a feature request (JRACLOUD-93971) aimed at finding alternatives or JEX language improvements for the above statement to simplify the evaluation for users. 
Engineer Note: Hi everyone, We’ve rolled out a fix for the issue described here. Previously, clearing a plain-text-rendered paragraph field on the modern transition screen could submit an invalid document. This could cause a workflow validator to fail even though the field appeared empty. The modern transition screen now submits a valid empty document when the field is cleared, addressing this validation failure. Please refresh Jira before retrying. This fix does not change how custom expressions should handle different rich-text formats; the format-aware emptiness expression shared in the previous update remains applicable. We’re resolving this issue as Fixed. If you still encounter the reported behaviour after refreshing, please contact Atlassian Support and reference this ticket so we can investigate your configuration. Thank you for your patience and for helping us investigate.

title: JCMA / Jira Cloud Ingestion fails to insert worklogs into Cloud database despite successful export and changelog creation
description: h3. Issue Summary When migrating Jira projects from Jira Server/Data Center to Jira Cloud using the Jira Cloud Migration Assistant (JCMA), worklogs are parsed and exported by JCMA, and the issue History / Changelog records the time spent increments and worklog IDs. However, the physical worklog entries are dropped / not inserted into the Jira Cloud } database table during Cloud batch ingestion. As a result: * The worklogs do not appear in the Jira Cloud issue view or worklog tabs. * REST API queries to the issue metadata ( GET /rest/api/3/issue/\ ?fields=worklog{}}}) show the correct non-zero total count from migration (e.g. total: 661{}}}), but calling the dedicated worklog endpoint ( GET /rest/api/3/issue/\ /worklog{}}}) returns an empty array ( worklogs: []{}}}, total: 0{}}}). * Monthly timesheet, billing, and worklog reports in third-party or native reporting tools fail to retrieve any worklog entries. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Migrate a Jira Server/Data Center project with extensive worklog history using JCMA. # Confirm that JCMA exports worklogs in the migration payload and completes with SUCCESS{}}}. # Open an affected migrated issue in Jira Cloud and inspect the Worklog tab / Issue History. # Call /worklog}} via REST API. h3. Expected Results All worklogs exported from Server/DC are inserted into the Jira Cloud database and visible via UI and REST API. h3. Actual Results * Issue history reflects that time spent was added with corresponding Worklog IDs, but the Worklog panel is empty. * /worklog}} returns 0 worklogs. * JCMA migration logs show no errors or warnings during container ingestion.   h3. Workaround Currently, there is no direct self-serve workaround. A backend database backfill / data fix script executed by Atlassian Database Operations / Engineering is required to re-insert the missing worklogs from the migration export payload into the Cloud tenant database.

title: Jira intermittently renders batch.css and batch.js resources on restarts after upgrade from 10.3.x to 11.3.x
description: h3. Issue Summary After an upgrade from 10.3.x to 11.3.x, Jira may intermittently fail to render batch.css and batch.js resources with content-type } while } is set to nosniff. * It has been observed on the  } endpoint that utilizes batch.css and batch.js files. * Authentication is NOT required. End users will see only an HTML page in their browser because the .css/.js files are not executed. * Restarting Jira on the node (or a Jira restart for single node systems) is required to clear the problem.   ** End users will then need to clear their browser cache completely if they hit the Jira node while this issue was present. ** If other users reached a node that was not having the issue, those users would not see the problem. Frequency : Generally after a nightly shutdown, backup, and restart, but it is not predictable.  h3. Steps to Reproduce We have not been able to reproduce this issue.  Running curl on the node directly for the batch.css file while the node had the issue produced a content type of application/octet-stream:   curl -v http://localhost:8080/jira/s/.../_/download/contextbatch/css/.../batch.css HTTP/1.1 200 ... X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff ... Content-Type: application/octet-stream;charset=UTF-8   After a node restart, the same batch.css resource displayed the correct content-type of text/css:   curl -v http://localhost:8080/jira/s/.../_/download/contextbatch/css/.../batch.css HTTP/1.1 200 ... X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff ... Content-Type: text/css;charset=UTF-8   h3. Expected Results Jira should serve the proper content-type for } (text/css) and } (application/javascript) files.  h3. Actual Results Jira intermittently serves } for batch.css and batch.js resources. h3. Workaround Current workaround: # Restart the affected node. # Any user who experienced the problem will need to clear their browser cache.

title: Out of date workflows may cause situations where Plans are unable to push changes live
description: h3. Issue Summary Currently, if a change to an issue's status within Plans Is made (but changes not committed), but then the workflow is _updated_ after these changes, Plans may end up still attempting to use the out of date workflow. This means that if the status it was changed to no longer exists, or potentially some other transition that no longer exists, it may "soft lock" the user from being able to commit any changes made on that issue/plan. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Update an issue's status within a plan, don't commit changes yet. # Change the workflow related to the issue's status that was changed and remove that status or transition to it and save the new workflow. # Attempt to commit changes set in step 1. h3. Expected Results Plans should be notifying the user that the status attempting to change into no longer exists/ask for a new one, or it should revoke the previously made changes and notify the user that the workflow was updated. h3. Actual Results The plan instead just states that a permissions error or some other error occurred. The below exception is thrown in the xxxxxxx.log file: ... h3. Workaround To get out of the soft lock, change the status into some other one that currently exists within the active workflow, commit the changes, then change it back if need be.

title: Moving an issue's dates in the Plans Calendar view on a non-default scenario applies the unsaved change to all scenarios instead of only the active scenario
description: h3. Issue Summary When using Jira Plans with multiple scenarios enabled, dragging an issue to reschedule it in the Calendar view while on a non-default scenario causes the pending (unsaved) change to appear in both the active scenario and the default scenario. Additionally, no colored change flags are displayed to indicate scenario-specific modifications. This effectively breaks scenario isolation in the Calendar view. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Create a Plan with at least one work item that has start and end dates # Enable Scenarios and create a second (non-default) scenario with a color assigned # Navigate to the Calendar tab while viewing the non-default scenario # Drag an issue to a new date range (or modify its dates inline) # Switch to the default scenario in the Calendar view h3. Expected Results * The date change should only appear as a pending change in the non-default scenario where it was made * A colored change flag (matching the scenario color) should appear on the modified item * The default scenario should remain unchanged until the user explicitly commits changes h3. Actual Results * The pending unsaved change appears in both the non-default and the default scenario * No colored scenario change flags are displayed on the modified item * Scenario isolation is not maintained in the Calendar view * The Unsaved change can only be submitted in the scenario where it was applied, and attempting to submit the change in the alternate scenario shows no changes available h3. Workaround Use the Timeline view to make scenario-specific date changes. Scenario isolation and colored change flags function correctly in the Timeline view. Avoid using the Calendar view for scenario planning until this is resolved. If you make multiple date changes between the two scenarios from the calendar view a Hard page refresh (Shift + Click on refresh in browser) is required to regain the ability to see and interact with the "Unsaved changes" in either scenario view

title: Reviewing bulk unsaved changes on a Plan causes staged status updates to silently disappear
description: h3. Issue Summary When reviewing approximately 25 unsaved changes on a Plan, staged status transitions silently disappear from the modal, resulting in only a subset of changes being saved. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Open a Plan that contains 20 or more issues. # On the Plan timeline/scope view, update the status for *21 existing issues* (do not save yet, keep them staged). # Create *4 new issues* inline directly within the Plan. # Click the *"Unsaved changes"* (or "Review changes") button in the top right corner to open the modal. Note : Once this issue occurs, it might not immediately happen again on consecutive attempts. However, reloading the browser page (F5 / Command+R) makes it reproducible again. h3. Expected Results All 25 staged changes (21 status updates and 4 newly created issues) remain listed and checked in the modal, allowing the user to click "Save changes" and commit all updates to Jira. h3. Actual Results * Immediately upon opening the modal, all 25 changes appear for about 1 second. However, right after that, the 21 status updates silently disappear from the list without any warning or error message, leaving only the 4 newly created issues. * As a result, clicking "Save changes" only commits the remaining 4 new issues, and the 21 status updates are lost and not saved to Jira. * This occurs even though permissions (Transition Issues), Issue Security, and workflow configurations (transition paths, screens, conditions, validators) are all valid.   h3. Workaround Save changes in smaller batches (e.g., save every 5–10 updates) rather than accumulating 20 or more unsaved changes at once on the Plan.

title: Backlog requests can cause OOMEs on Lucene by retaining unbounded search results in memory
description: h3. Issue Summary On Jira Software 10.7.0+ using Lucene, loading a rapid board backlog can retain a very large number of issue documents in memory and cause an OutOfMemoryError. The rapid board search uses a batch-oriented search API. When the effective Lucene result window is unlimited, the request loads the selected fields for all matching issues into an in-memory SearchResponse before Jira Software processes them into backlog entries. This can affect requests to: /rest/greenhopper/1.0/xboard/plan/backlog/data.json The result limit passed by Jira Software is based on the search platform maximum result window. On Lucene, this remains effectively unlimited unless the Lucene search-limit dark feature is enabled. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Use Jira Software with Lucene as the search platform # Create or use a rapid board whose backlog search has a very large candidate result set # Load the board backlog, or send a request to: /rest/greenhopper/1.0/xboard/plan/backlog/data.json # Repeat the request concurrently or refresh the backlog page while the original request is still running # Observe heap usage or capture a heap dump while the requests are in progress h3. Expected Results The backlog request should use bounded or streaming processing. The request should not retain selected Lucene document fields for every matching issue at the same time. The configured search result window should protect both OpenSearch and Lucene deployments. h3. Actual Results The backlog request can use an effective result window of } on Lucene. Jira Software loads selected fields for _all matching issues_ into SearchHit objects and retains them in the SearchResponse before processing the results into RapidIssueEntry objects. On a large instance, a single request can retain many gigabytes of heap. Multiple concurrent requests, for example after a user refreshes a stalled backlog page, can exhaust the Java heap and terminate the node. The below exception is thrown in the atlassian-jira.log file: java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space h3. Workaround Enable the Lucene search-result limit dark feature: com.atlassian.jira.lucene.search.limit.enabled This applies the configured search platform maximum result window to all Lucene search requests on the Jira instance, not only Jira Software rapid-board backlog requests. The default maximum result window is 10,000 results. Administrators should assess the effect on integrations, apps, and custom workloads that currently request more than the configured result window.

title: OpenSearch node skips Lucene updates during ZDU migration
