title: Upgrading Jira Data Center to version 11.x on an existing index results in startup failure due to DocValues type mismatch
description:
Jira 11.3.12 introduces a new parameter: -Dcom.atlassian.jira.startup.lucene.skip.index.recovery=true Default: false{}}}. When set to true{}}}, Jira skips Lucene index recovery entirely during startup. The index is neither validated nor recovered, and the node is allowed to start. Index replication stays paused on that node, so it will not apply index updates coming from other nodes. h4. How to upgrade from 10.x to 11.x using the property # Back up your database, shared home and local home. Note that 10.x → 11.x is a major platform upgrade and cannot be done as a rolling (zero downtime) upgrade. # Shut down *all* nodes in the cluster. # Upgrade the binaries on node 1 to 11.x and add the property to that node's JVM arguments (in } / setenv.bat{}}}, via JVM_SUPPORT_RECOMMENDED_ARGS{}}}). # Start node 1 only . It will log a warning that index recovery was skipped, then reach a running state. The upgrade tasks execute and the build number in the database advances to 11.x. # Run a full foreground re-index : Administration → System → Indexing → Full re-index{}}}, option "Lock Jira and rebuild index" . Do not use the background re-index, it cannot repair an index with incompatible field types and will fail part way through. # When the re-index finishes, shut down node 1, remove the property , and start node 1 again. It will now start through the normal index path. # Before starting the remaining nodes, remove the pre-upgrade index snapshots from the shared home so that those nodes cannot restore a 10.x index. Then start nodes 2..N one at a time, *without* the property. h4. Notes * Do not leave the property enabled in normal operation. A node running with a skipped index recovery is not in a supported state. Thank you for your patience while we worked through this one. Konrad Plasota Software Engineer h3. Issue Summary When upgrading Jira Data Center from version 10.x to 11.x, the application may fail to start or experience significant functional degradation (broken gadgets, missing side panels, failed webhooks) due to an index incompatibility. Specifically, Jira 11 introduces breaking changes to how subtasks and issue properties are indexed (switching from } to SORTED_SET{}}}). If Jira attempts to reuse or incrementally update an existing Jira 10 index, it throws an IllegalArgumentException{}}}, which subsequently blocks the } and prevents the } from firing. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Install Jira Data Center version 10.3.x and create issues with subtasks. # Perform an upgrade to Jira Data Center version 11.3.x. # Start the Jira 11 instance using the existing Jira 10 index without performing a full re-index. # Observe the startup logs and application behavior. h3. Expected Results Jira should either automatically detect the index version mismatch and force a full re-index, or provide a clear upgrade task/documentation requiring a full re-index to prevent startup failure. h3. Actual Results Jira fails to run upgrade tasks and initialize the index correctly. The below exception is thrown in the } file: main ERROR [c.a.jira.upgrade.UpgradeLauncher] Skipping, JIRA is locked. main INFO [c.a.jira.scheduler.JiraSchedulerLauncher] JIRA Scheduler not started: JIRA startup failed. main INFO [c.a.jira.scheduler.JiraSchedulerLauncher] The following failures prevent Jira from being started: main INFO [c.a.jira.scheduler.JiraSchedulerLauncher] (Event: Level = (EventLevel: warning) , Key = (EventType: no-index) , Desc = We could not find a valid search index on the current node , Exception = Jira needs to have a valid search index after starting. During the node startup, all of the following steps failed to pass:
  • Re-index missing data if a local issue index is less than 10% behind the database.
  • Check if Jira shared-home directory contains a recent index snapshot.
  • Trigger a full re-index.
You need to fix this issue manually. Do not start other nodes until the indexing problem is resolved. ) main INFO [c.a.jira.startup.LauncherContextListener] Startup is complete. Jira is ready to serve. IssueIndexer:thread-2 WARN [c.a.jira.index.AccumulatingResultBuilder] Indexing failed for Issue - '100000' IssueIndexer:thread-2 WARN [c.a.jira.index.AccumulatingResultBuilder] cannot change DocValues type from SORTED_NUMERIC to SORTED_SET for field "issue_subtasks" java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: cannot change DocValues type from SORTED_NUMERIC to SORTED_SET for field "issue_subtasks" at org.apache.lucene.index.FieldInfos$FieldNumbers.verifyConsistent(FieldInfos.java:289) at org.apache.lucene.index.FieldInfos$FieldNumbers.setDocValuesType(FieldInfos.java:337) ... IssueIndexer:thread-3 WARN [c.a.jira.index.AccumulatingResultBuilder] Indexing failed for Issue - '100000' IssueIndexer:thread-3 WARN [c.a.jira.index.AccumulatingResultBuilder] cannot change DocValues type from SORTED to SORTED_SET for field "ISSUEPROP_jpo-issue-properties$baseline_start" java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: cannot change DocValues type from SORTED to SORTED_SET for field "ISSUEPROP_jpo-issue-properties$baseline_start" at org.apache.lucene.index.FieldInfos$FieldNumbers.verifyConsistent(FieldInfos.java:289) at org.apache.lucene.index.FieldInfos$FieldNumbers.setDocValuesType(FieldInfos.java:337) ... Upgrade task banner and dashboard gadget broken: !failed-upgrade-task-banner.png|width=790,height=300! h3. Workaround To resolve this, you must force Jira to perform a full re-index on startup by bypassing the local index and shared snapshots. Add the following JVM arguments to your Jira startup configuration: -Dcom.atlassian.jira.startup.rebuild.local.index=false -Dcom.atlassian.jira.startup.pick.indexsnapshot.from.shared=false -Dcom.atlassian.jira.startup.allow.full.reindex=true *Note:* Ensure only one node is started initially to perform the full re-index before joining other nodes to the cluster.
comment:
Engineer Note: The more severe effect of this is that customers may be forced down a double-index path: # Disable plugins that are incompatible with new Jira version # Upgrade Jira, let it full reindex # Upgrade plugins # Reindex again Many customer runbooks use this order. Perhaps it could be shifted: # Upgrade plugins # Upgrade Jira, let it full reindex However not all plugins are compatible with the new major version - it's a common pattern for vendors to have separate plugin versions for major Jira versions In that case, the double index path is hit, significantly increasing the upgrade window. It is common to see 4hr - 8hr reindex performance, so it can blow out an upgrade from 1 day to days.
Engineer Note: We reduced the needed time for the upgrade massively by deinstalling the plugins before the upgrade from 10 to 11 and install them afterwards already with the versions for Jira 11 - saves a lot of time stopping/starting the application server, no problems with the different changes from 10 to 11 for the plugins, and also reducing the log entries for the plugins.

title: Restarting nodes replciates JiraDelegatingDirectoryInstanceLoader cache causing HIGH IOPS and outage
description: h3. Issue Summary Cluster-wide invalidation loop in } cache causes high CPU and log volume during production load or rolling restarts. *Background:* The cache } is initialized without a CacheLoader{}}}. This causes } to treat it as a non-self-loading cache, setting replicateUpdates=true{}}}. Because the cache is not self-loading, it lacks the SynchronizedLoadingCacheDecorator{}}}. Under production load, concurrent misses on the same key result in multiple threads loading the same entry in parallel. Each subsequent } is classified as an *UPDATE* and broadcast as a cluster-wide invalidation message to all peer nodes. This creates a self-sustaining feedback loop: * *Node A* misses, repopulates, and broadcasts an invalidation. * *Nodes B through F* evict the entry. * *Nodes B through F* then miss, repopulate, and broadcast invalidations back to Node A . * *Node A* evicts, and the cycle repeats indefinitely. A node with a cold cache (e.g., during a rolling restart) acts as the strongest invalidation source, often worsening the incident until a full cluster cold restart is performed. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Run a Jira Data Center cluster under high concurrency. # Perform a rolling restart of one node and observe the increase in invalidation traffic on peer nodes. # Observe the volume of invalidation messages and CPU spikes across nodes. *Note* This issue is was consistently reproducible during high concurrency and restart of nodes. h3. Expected Results Cache repopulation should be synchronized and should not trigger cluster-wide invalidations for ordinary reads. h3. Actual Results Concurrent misses trigger multiple "UPDATE" events, leading to a cluster-wide invalidation storm and high log volume (specifically from TapeLocalQCacheOpQueue{}}}). Stacktrace of the threads stuck on I/O attempting to  write JiraDelegatingDirectoryInstanceLoader cache to the localQ causing high load and incrased I/O activity. at title: Performance degradation in Jira 11.3 due to serializing application property reads
description: h3. Issue Summary In Jira 11.3.x, concurrent reads of application properties can block each other and slow down the whole Jira instance. Jira uses a component to choose how it reads application properties before and after database setup. For each property read, this component calls }. This method takes the local } and checks the database configuration. Only one thread can run this check at a time. The problem is most visible when code reads an application property many times. One example is the read-only mode check in permission checks. Jira 11.3 runs this check during issue, project, and project-wide permission checks. Read-only mode is only one trigger. It is not the root cause. Disabling read-only mode does not help because Jira still needs to read the property to check whether the mode is enabled. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Use Jira Data Center 11.3.x # Run many operations at the same time that perform issue or project permission checks ## For example, run large JQL searches, Structure jobs, or Zephyr Scale imports or reports at the same time # Collect 5 to 10 thread dumps, 10 seconds apart, while the workload is running # Check the thread dumps for threads waiting in } h3. Expected Results Concurrent application property reads do not block each other. Permission-heavy work does not cause lock-related delays across the Jira instance. h3. Actual Results Application property reads can wait for }. When many threads read application properties at the same time, they wait for } to finish and execute the check one thread at a time. This can increase request time and cause Jira to become slow across the instance. h3. Workaround * Stagger large 3rd-party app processing jobs instead of running them concurrently. * Reduce or reschedule operations that perform large project-wide or issue-wide permission enumerations. * Avoid running large permission-heavy background jobs during peak interactive usage.
comment: Engineer Note: We would like to emphasize that this issue is critically blocking our business operations. Since upgrading to Jira 11.3.x, we have been facing severe performance problems that align with the lock contention described in this bug report. The resulting application slowness is having a substantial impact on thousands of users across our Jira environment. Given the business impact, we kindly request that Atlassian prioritize this investigation and provide guidance on potential mitigation steps or an estimated target release for a fix.

title: OpenSearch index lags when migrating from Lucene in Jira DC
description: h3. Issue Summary While migrating from Lucene to OpenSearch via the zero-downtime method ([Migrating to OpenSearch without downtime|https://confluence.atlassian.com/adminjiraserver/migrating-to-opensearch-without-downtime-1671102827.html]), the OpenSearch dark node may fall behind on changes produced by the Lucene nodes. When Jira is running in either Lucene/OpenSearch hybrid mode or full OpenSearch mode, pending changes are committed to the OpenSearch index via the } (similar to the } for Lucene). Since the OpenSearch index is a shared resource, this is a "once per cluster" job. However, Lucene nodes delegate to }, which does not actually register a job runner. Clustered jobs running with Atlassian Scheduler have nondeterministic node assignment, so a Lucene node may execute the job. When execution reaches a Lucene node, an error is logged, and pending changes are not committed to the OpenSearch index. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Set up a 2-node Jira cluster: ## One Lucene node ## One OpenSearch (dark) node # Enable the } feature flag. # Reindex the OpenSearch node to generate an initial index and register the } job runner. # Update some issues from the Lucene node. # Wait ~5 minutes. h3. Expected Results Issue index changes produced by the Lucene node are quickly processed by the OpenSearch node when the job runs (once a minute). No errors appear in the logs. h3. Actual Results The following appears in the Lucene node's }: 2026-09-21 21:00:00,000+0000 Caesium-1-1 WARN anonymous [c.a.scheduler.core.AbstractSchedulerService] Job 'com.atlassian.jira.search.index.rio.DefaultOpenSearchIndexReplayService' completed with non-success outcome: outcome=UNAVAILABLE durationMs=3 message='Job runner key 'com.atlassian.jira.search.index.rio.DefaultOpenSearchIndexReplayService' is not registered' At ⚙️ (gear icon) > *System* > *Scheduler details* (either node): !scheduler-failure.png|width=600! For as long as the execution lands on a Lucene node, the OpenSearch index will lag. h3. Workaround There is no workaround, but the incidence will decrease as more nodes are migrated from Lucene to OpenSearch. The problem will clear when the cluster is fully migrated to OpenSearch.

title: Jira Logging and Profiling UI displays a "root" logger at DEBUG level starting in Jira 11.3.5
description: h3. Issue Summary Starting with Jira 11.3.5 , the *Logging and Profiling* administration page displays a named logger called } with a default level of DEBUG{}}}. description: h3. Issue Summary When running the Custom Field Optimizer (CFO), it won't show that projects with archived issues are using the target custom field, nor that they may be part of the change applied by the optimizer. h3. title: Clearing the entire CHANGE_HISTORY entityVersionCache on each issue delete causes repeated expensive Lucene lookups and cluster‑wide performance degradation
description: h3. Issue Summary *CHANGE_HISTORY* *entityVersionCache* is fully cleared on each issue delete, causing repeated expensive Lucene BKD lookups and severe performance degradation on memory‑constrained, large Jira Data Center clusters. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Set up a Jira Data Center cluster with: ** Large heap (e.g., 50 GB) and limited remaining system RAM (so that OS page cache is tight). # Warm up the CHANGE_HISTORY entityVersionCache by performing normal issue operations (create/update) and observe: ** Reasonable cache hit rates. ** Low replaceDocumentsWithVersionMillis (few ms). # Start deleting issues at a moderate rate from multiple nodes/users during peak activity. h3. Expected Results * Deleting an issue should invalidate/evict only the cache entries relevant to that issue (or at least minimally necessary entries), not the whole cache. * Avoid causing cluster-wide cache wipes for unrelated entities. h3. Actual Results * WriterWrapper.deleteDocuments() clears the entire entityVersionCache whenever an issue is deleted. * In a cluster, this cache clear is replicated to all nodes. * Under steady or bursty deletion patterns, caches on some nodes rarely warm up, forcing frequent disk‑backed BKD tree lookups for CHANGE_HISTORY updates, resulting in high latency and node health issues. h3. Workaround These are operational mitigations, not fixes for the code‑level bug: * Reduce JVM heap to free OS page cache ( Primary Mitigation ) * Operational guidance around issue deletions ( Secondary Mitigation ) ** Advise users to avoid concentrated bursts of deletions during peak hours . ** Encourage bulk cleanup (e.g., backlog grooming, mass deletions) to be performed *outside peak business hours*
comment: Engineer Note: The fix has been implemented behind a dark feature flag, com.atlassian.jira.index.version.check.without.range.query, which is turned OFF by default on 10.3.x and 11.3.x, and ON by default in Jira 12.x. This means that on 10.3.x and 11.3.x you need to enable it manually, while on Jira 12.x no action is required. If you have any questions, please contact support.

title: Remote issue link picker returns empty results when the current Cloud project key doesn't exist on the linked DC instance
description: h3. Issue Summary When creating a remote issue link from Jira Cloud to a linked Jira DC instance (via Application Tunnel), the remote issue picker dropdown returns empty results. The picker passes the current Cloud project key as a context filter to the DC instance's } endpoint. If the Cloud project key does not exist on DC, the search returns no results, and the dropdown appears empty. Typing the full issue key (e.g., PROJ-123) and submitting works only affects the autocomplete/search dropdown{}}}. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Set up an Application Link between Jira Cloud and Jira DC using Application Tunnel # On Jira DC, open an issue in a project (e.g., project key TEST{}}}) # Click *Link* → select the linked DC instance as the remote server # Start typing in the issue search field to search for DC issues # Observe: the dropdown shows no results h3. Expected Results The remote issue picker dropdown should return matching issues from the DC instance regardless of whether the current Cloud project key exists on DC. The Cloud project key should not be sent as a mandatory filter to the DC picker endpoint. h3. Actual Results * The Jira DC picker forwards its currentJQL (for example, project = SC) to the linked Cloud instance. The Cloud search applies it as a mandatory filter, so an existing Cloud issue is excluded because it is not in Cloud project SC. * Since project } does not exist on Cloud, the query returns empty results * The dropdown shows nothing * Typing the full issue key and submitting works correctly h3. Workaround # Go to *Issues* from the top navigation bar # Click *Current search* # *Deselect any project* that is currently selected/checked in the filters # Try the remote issue link search again. The dropdown will now populate correctly

title: Cloud Site Import / Backup & Restore removes https:// prefix from destination URLs in comments and text fields during URL replacement
description: h3. Issue Summary When importing data using Jira Cloud Backup & Restore / Site Import with the option to replace the source site URL with the destination site URL, the replacement logic strips the https:// protocol prefix. As a result, destination URLs in comments and text fields become incomplete (e.g., destination-site.atlassian.net/browse/... instead of https://destination-site.atlassian.net/browse/...), preventing them from rendering as clickable smartlinks or markdown links. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Take a site backup containing Jira work items with comments or custom text fields linking to the source site (e.g., https://source-site.atlassian.net/browse/ABC-123). # Perform a Cloud Site Import / Backup & Restore into a destination Jira Cloud instance. # Configure the URL replacement to map the source site URL to the destination site URL. # Inspect imported work items, comments, and text fields where the source site URLs were replaced. h3. Expected Results Source site URLs are replaced with the full destination URL including the https:// protocol (e.g., https://destination-site.atlassian.net/browse/ABC-123), and links render as clickable hyperlinks/smartlinks. h3. Actual Results The https:// prefix is removed during replacement, leaving bare URLs (e.g., destination-site.atlassian.net/browse/ABC-123). These are not parsed as valid links and remain plain, unclickable text. h3. Workaround Currently, there is no native workaround post-import other than manually editing or using API scripts to update comments and text fields to prepend https://.

title: Group picker search remains case-sensitive for accented / diacritic characters (regression of JRACLOUD-78490)
description: h3. Issue Summary Following the rollout of JRACLOUD-78490, case-insensitive searching in group picker fields works for standard English characters. However, searching remains case-sensitive when using lowercase accented / diacritic characters. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Create a group containing diacritic characters (e.g., Test - Škultéty{}}}). # Open a JSM work item with a group picker field (e.g., Multi-Group Picker). # Attempt to search for the group using lowercase diacritics (e.g., type škul{}}}). # Attempt to search for the group using proper case / uppercase (e.g., type Škul{}}}). h3. Expected Results Searching for } returns } (case-insensitive match). h3. Actual Results Searching for } returns no results . Searching for } correctly returns the group. h3. Workaround Users must match the exact capitalization of accented characters when typing in group picker fields.

title: Saving a Jira Plans view with an expanded label group containing a hyphen causes the group to appear collapsed when the view is reopened
description: h3. Issue Summary When a Jira Plans view is grouped by Label or Component, expanded groups with hyphens in their names are not preserved when the current view is saved. h3. Steps to Reproduce 1. Open a plan and group the timeline by Label. 2. Create a label group with a hyphenated name, for example, “High-priority work”. 3. Expand the label group. 4. Select “Save current view” and confirm the save. 5. Reload the page, or switch to another view and return to the saved view. h3. Expected Results The group remains expanded.  h3. Actual Results After reloading or returning to the saved view, the group is collapsed. h3. Workaround Rename the affected group so that its name does not contain a hyphen before saving the view. For example, use “High priority work” instead of “High-priority work”.

title: When a child issue is created under an existing parent, the "Issue Updated" webhook event is triggered before the "Issue Created" event
description: h3. Issue Summary Creating a child issue under an existing parent triggers the update Webhook event before the create event h3. Steps to Reproduce # Create an Epic issue # Create a child issue under the Epic issue # Use a webhook inspector or an add-on application that relies on Jira webhook triggers h3. Expected Results _Issue_ _Created_ webhook event should be triggered before the _Issue_ _updated_ webhook event. h3. Actual Results _Issue_ _updated_ __ webhook event _is triggered before the _Issue_ _Created_  webhook event. h3. Workaround Create the child issue first and then edit the parent field to make sure that the _Issue_ _Created_ will be triggered first.
comment: Engineer Note: Multiple Webhook Triggers on Subtask Creation When a subtask is created, we receive two webhook requests at the same time: webhookEvent: jira:issue_created issue_event_type_name: issue_created webhookEvent: jira:issue_updated issue_event_type_name: issue_updated Because both events are triggered simultaneously for the same subtask, this results in duplicate processing and makes it difficult to reliably extract data from the correct record.

title: Creating an issue via List view inline create shows a due date validation error when jira.date.picker.java.format is set to a non-default value

title: SLA custom field fails to update dynamically in Filter Results (User-specific / Intermittent)
description: h3. Issue Summary SLA custom field time fails to update dynamically in the *Filter Results* view for specific users, while other users on the same instance view the updated values correctly. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Open an *Issue Search / Filter view* containing tickets with an active SLA field column displayed. # Note the remaining SLA time displayed in the column (e.g., "50 minutes"). # Wait for few minutes (e.g., 5–10 minutes). # Refresh the Filter view page multiple times and observe the SLA column. # Search for or view the same tickets in a different filter/issue search view. # Compare the displayed SLA time directly against the actual SLA time shown on the *Issue View* or in Jira Service Management (JSM) Queues . h3. Expected Results The SLA time column in the Filter Results view should update dynamically to reflect the actual remaining SLA time upon page refresh. h3. Actual Results * *Affected Users:* The SLA time values in the Filter Results view columns remain static indefinitely or take several hours to update, regardless of page refreshes. * *Unaffected Users:* Other users viewing the same filter/tickets see the updated SLA time promptly or within a few minutes. h3. Workaround Check the SLA time directly on the *Issue View* page or view the ticket within JSM Queues .

title: Changing security level of an issue parent with an automation sometimes leads to subtasks not reflecting new security level
description: h3. Issue Summary In rare cases it has been observed that when using automations to create subtasks and setting the security level of the parent using a different automation rule, the first subtask created may not inherit the new security level of the parent. This issue has been split out from [JRACLOUD-84875|https://jira.atlassian.com/browse/JRACLOUD-84875] to help gather information about how widespread this issue is, and what the conditions are to produce it. h3. Steps to Reproduce Difficult to pin down specific steps at this stage. h3. Expected Results The subtask issue should inherit the new security level of the parent. h3. Actual Results The subtask is stuck with the old security level of the parent before automation changed it. h3. Workaround Change the security level of the parent again manually, without using an automation.

title: Switching to a Plan view grouped by Goal does not display the Goal-based groups
description: h3. Issue Summary Grouping a Jira Plan by Goals does not create the expected Goal-based groups. All issues are placed under "All Other issues". h3. Steps to Reproduce # Open Jira Plan with a view where the Goals column is not displayed and issues are not grouped by Goal. # Switch to another view where the Goals column is also not displayed, but issues are grouped by Goal. h3. Expected Results Issues are grouped under their associated goals based on the values populated in the Goal field. h3. Actual Results All issues are placed under “All Other issues” group. h3. title: fixVersion inaccurate JQL results
description: h3. Issue Summary JQL filters in Jira Cloud are returning inaccurate results when filtering by fixVersion{}}}. Specifically, issues assigned to a different version (e.g., 5.1.22{}}}) are appearing in search results for a specific version (e.g., fixVersion = 5.1.21{}}}). h3. title: In old transition experience, setting a workflow validator on the Parent field is not picking up the Parent field properly
description: h3. Issue Summary In the Old Transition experience, setting a workflow validator on the Parent field is not picking up the Parent field properly. Note: This is reproducible in the Old Transition Experience only h3. Steps to Reproduce * Configure a workflow transition with the workflow validator that checks if Parent field is not empty ** In the same transition, add transition screen that includes the Parent field. * If the Parent field is not in the transition screen, the validator works (it can see if the parent field is filled up) (/) * If the Parent field is in the transition screen, the validator keeps saying the Parent field is empty. (x) * If there is no transition screen, the validator can read the Parent field. (/) h3. Expected Results The validator should recognise the updated Parent value provided on the transition screen and allow the transition to proceed. h3. Actual Results The validator continues to block the transition regardless of whether the Parent field is filled up before the transition, or whether it has been updated in the transition screen. h3. Workaround Several options: * Remove the transition screen for that workflow transition. * Remove the Parent field from the transition screen for that workflow transition. Instruct users to update the Parent field directly on the issue view page before initiating the transition. The validator should recognise the updated Parent value provided on the transition screen and allow the transition to proceed. * Create a support ticket to move over to modernized transition will also resolve this behaviour as the fix has been deployed there. [JRACLOUD-99266: Native "Field Required" validator fails to recognise updates (clearing field) following the enablement of the Modern Transition Screen Experience|https://jira.atlassian.com/browse/JRACLOUD-99266] * For validators that check if a field is empty: Optional workaround is to use *Matches regular expression* for the validator, and use below REGEX for the field. This is the exact same behaviour as choosing the *Isn't empty* validator. .*+

title: Inconsistent Display of Child Work Items in Epic Due to Hierarchy Changes
description: h3. Issue Summary Child work items are not displayed under their Epic parent in the Work view if the child’s work type is moved to a higher hierarchy level than Epic. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Add a child work item to an Epic. # Change the Work Type Hierarchy so that the child’s work type is now at a higher level than Epic. # Open the Epic and check the *Child Work Items* section. h3. Expected Results All child work items should be visible under the Epic, regardless of changes to the work type hierarchy. The display should be consistent before and after the hierarchy change. h3. Actual Results * The child work item is missing from the *Child Work Items* section. * If you click the three dots ("...") and toggle the "Hide Done" checkbox, all child items become visible. h3. Workaround Move the child work item’s work type back to a level below Epic in the Work Type Hierarchy.

title: Create linked work item from JSW to JSM clears the Linked Issue field when Simple Create is ON
description: h3. Issue Summary When using "+ Create linked work item" from a Jira Software (JSW) issue to create a linked item in a Jira Service Management (JSM) project, the Linked Issue field is cleared/empty on the modernized (Simple Create) issue create screen. The linked issue field value that should be pre-populated is lost when the create dialog opens. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Open any work item in a Jira Software project. # In the *Linked Issues* section, click "+ Create linked work item" # In the create dialog, change the project to a JSM project. # Observe the *Linked Issue* field - it is empty. h3. Expected Results The *Linked Issue* field should be pre-populated with the originating JSW work item, just as it works when creating a linked item from within a JSM project.  h3. Actual Results The Linked Issue field is blank/cleared when creating a linked work item from JSW → JSM with the modernized issue create screen (Simple Create ON). h3. Workaround Perform the following steps to turn off *Simple Create as default* * Navigate to *Settings* → *System* → *General Configuration* * Click on *Edit Settings* and turn off Simple Create as the default . * Click on *Update* to save the changes The linked issue field is correctly populated when Simple Create is disabled.

title: Increasing the number of custom filters in team-managed will make them unavailable on the board list

Issue Summary if you add a big number of custom filters in your team-managed space, in a way that the list gets bigger enough to not display entirely on the screen, the last ones you add will not be displayed on the board list to be selected. title: Attempting to create a Space with Shared Settings does not work as expected
description: h3. Issue Summary When attempting to create a Space using the Shared Settings option, there is a condition that exists that causes the checkbox to uncheck when selecting the 'Create' button without telling the user and the Space is then just created with the defaults. h3. title: Story Points field clears from Jira Plan UI after saving changes via "Review changes" modal until page refresh
description: h3. Issue Summary When updating the *Story Points* field via inline-edit within a Jira Plan view and saving the update using the *Review changes > Save selected changes* modal, the UI fails to render the updated value and instead shows the field as blank/empty. The backend update is successful: opening the issue detail view or performing a hard browser refresh displays the updated Story Points value correctly.  h3. Steps to Reproduce # Navigate to *Plans* in Jira Cloud and open an existing Plan (e.g., Timeline or Scope/Sprint Planning view). # Locate any issue and *inline-edit the Story Points* field with a new numerical value. # In the top-right warning bar, click Review changes . # In the modal, click Save selected changes . # Observe the Story Points column/field for that issue in the Plan view. # Refresh the browser page ( Cmd + R{}}} / Ctrl + F5{}}}) or open the issue details panel h3. Expected Results Upon clicking Save selected changes , the Plan UI should immediately update and display the newly saved Story Points value without requiring a browser refresh. h3. Actual Results The Story Points value disappears/clears from the Plan UI immediately after saving. The updated estimate only appears after manually refreshing the browser page. h3. Workaround * Perform a hard refresh ( Cmd + Shift + R{}}} / Ctrl + F5{}}}) of the browser page after saving changes to reflect the updated Story Points.

Issue Summary Any interactions with the "View Settings -> Group By" functionality will be interpreted as a "View" edition, even if there were no changes performed in the Group By tab. Steps to Reproduce # Create an Advanced Roadmaps Plan # Create some label groups in View Settings -> Group By -> Label -> Create Group # Add some labels inside each group so you can expand them later # After creating the groups, save your Plan View # Now, go back to your View Settings -> Group By -> Label, and try expanding any created groups. # Jira will interpret that you performed a change, and the View will show as 'Edited'. h3. Expected Results If the user has not really changed or updated the View Settings at all, only clicked through the options, it shouldn't be interpreted as an edition action.   h3. Actual Results Currently, it is interpreted as an edition action. h3. Workaround Currently there is no known workaround for this behavior. A workaround will be added here when available

title: Intermittent behaviour with Σ Original Estimate/Σ Remaining Estimate issue calculation
description: h3. Issue Summary Intermittent behaviour with the Σ Original Estimate/Σ Remaining Estimate issue calculation When we open an epic or story and add the field Σ Original Estimate/Σ Remaining Estimate, it first shows the data for a while; however, as soon as we refresh, the data is gone. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Create an epic-type issue. # Create a two-story type issue and set the original estimate. # Create a subtask under each story and set the original estimate for it. # Now, under the story, add the columns Σ Original Estimate. This will reflect the value under the  Σ Original Estimate for a while, and as soon as we refresh it's gone. # Similar behaviour is happening for Epic as well. Similar behaviour is being noticed for ΣRemaining estimate.   h3. Expected Results  Σ Original Estimate/Σ Remaining Estimate should show the result consistently h3. Actual Results When we open an epic or story and add the field Σ Remaining Estimate/Σ Original Estimate, it first shows the data for a while; however, as soon as we refresh, the data is gone. h3. Workaround 1) Go to the list view, add the field Σ Original Estimate/Σ Remaing Estimate in the columns and filter by work item type, then select your issue type, for example, story or epic. 2) Marketplace app Epic sum
comment:
Engineer Note: I would also like to provide feedback regarding *JRACLOUD-99194* and the currently proposed workarounds. h3. Workarounds Unfortunately, the first workaround does not really solve the issue for our workflow. Using the List view , manually adding the *Σ Original Estimate* column, filtering by work item type, and then locating the required Story or Epic only provides an alternative place where the value may be viewed. It does not restore the expected behavior inside the Story/Epic hierarchy where we actually need to work with these estimates. Therefore, I would consider this a limited way to access the data rather than a practical workaround for the issue. The second workaround — using the *Epic Sum Marketplace app* — is also not convenient for us. Introducing and maintaining an additional third-party application just to compensate for inconsistent behavior of Jira's native estimation fields is not a suitable solution for our workflow. h3. Bug priority I also noticed that JRACLOUD-99194 is currently marked as Low priority . Could you please reconsider the priority or impact level of this bug? For us, this affects a core Jira functionality used for planning and tracking estimates across the hierarchy: *Sub-task → Story → Epic* The issue makes the native aggregated estimation data unreliable in the UI and forces us to introduce additional Automation rules and other workarounds to maintain and access information that Jira already calculates. Considering that neither of the currently proposed workarounds provides an equivalent replacement for the expected native behavior, I believe the current *Low* priority may underestimate the practical impact of the issue. h3. Remaining Estimate should also be included Finally, please add an important clarification to the bug context: *The problem is not limited to Σ Original Estimate. We are also experiencing the issue with the aggregated Remaining Estimate / Σ Remaining Estimate.* The current JRACLOUD-99194 description only mentions *Σ Original Estimate* in the Issue Summary, Steps to Reproduce, Expected Results, and Actual Results. Please either: * update *JRACLOUD-99194* to explicitly include the *Remaining Estimate / Σ Remaining Estimate* behavior as part of the affected functionality, or * create a separate bug for Remaining Estimate if Atlassian considers it a separate issue. It is important for us that the Remaining Estimate problem is formally tracked and not lost because the current bug description only refers to Original Estimate. Thank you, and I would appreciate it if you could also reconsider the current priority based on the broader impact described above.
Engineer Note: A fix for this bug has been made and will be rolled out to each region today.

title: Modernized board : Combining custom Quick Filters containing OR conditions with toolbar filters fails due to missing parentheses
description: h3. Issue Summary When using the new [Mordanized Board|https://community.atlassian.com/forums/Jira-articles/Upcoming-Modernised-Software-boards-in-Jira-Company-Managed/ba-p/3275952] view in Jira Software (Company-Managed single-space projects), combining a toolbar filter (such as Assignee) with a custom Quick Filter that uses an `OR` condition results in unexpected filtering behavior. The board combines the UI filters and the Quick Filter JQL with an `AND` operator without wrapping the Quick Filter clause in parentheses. Due to JQL operator precedence (`AND` evaluated before `OR`), the query evaluates as: `(assignee = user AND condition1) OR condition2` rather than: `assignee = user AND (condition1 OR condition2) h3. Steps to Reproduce # Enable the Harmonised Board view on a Company-Managed Software board. # Create a Quick Filter with an OR condition, e.g., `resolution = Unresolved OR updatedDate >= -1d`.   # On the board, select a specific user from the **Assignee** dropdown filter. #  Activate the Quick Filter. h3. Expected Results The board displays only tickets assigned to the selected user that match either `resolution = Unresolved` OR `updatedDate >= -1d`. h3. Actual Results The board displays all tickets updated in the last 24 hours (`updatedDate >= -1d`) regardless of assignee, because the query is evaluated as `(assignee = user AND resolution = Unresolved) OR updatedDate >= -1d`. h3. Workaround Currently there is no known workaround for this behavior. A workaround will be added here when available
comment: Engineer Note: Hi folks, the fix for this bug is now fully deployed and the bug should be resolved. Please let me know if you're still seeing unexpected behaviour with quick filters.

title: Native "Field Required" validator fails to recognise updates (clearing field) following the enablement of the Modern Transition Screen Experience
description: h3. Issue Summary When a workflow transition is configured with a native Jira validator (e.g., "Field Required" or "Validate a field") targeting the *Parent* field (or potentially others), the validator fails to block the transition if the field is updated/cleared directly on the  Transition Screen . The validator appears to evaluate the issue's state _before_ the transition screen updates are applied, rather than validating the new values provided during the transition. *Note: This is reproducible in the New/Modern Transition Experience (this is not reproducible in the Old Transition Screen experience - [https://community.atlassian.com/t5/Jira-articles/Now-GA-try-the-new-issue-transition-experience-in-Jira/ba-p/2734436]*  h3. Steps to Reproduce # Ensure the *New Modern Transition Screen* experience is enabled for the site # Configure a workflow transition with a validator (e.g., Field Required ) for the *Parent* field. # Take a work item that currently *has* a Parent value. # Trigger the transition to open the transition screen. # On the transition screen, *clear* the Parent field. # Click the transition button (e.g., "Update" or "Done"). h3. Expected Results The validator should identify that the Parent field is now empty and block the transition with an error message. h3. Actual Results The transition succeeds. The validator treats the field as if it still contains the pre-transition value. h3. Workaround Currently there is no known workaround for this behaviour. A workaround will be added here when available
comment:
Engineer Note: I'm getting tons of user reports now telling me that our regex validator on the Parent field is failing even though it previously worked without problems. Please prioritise! This is a regression that affects a whole department in our company. For some reason I got reports from multiple people starting September 10. The only solution is to clear the Parent field before the transition or, as I have learned now, to switch back to the old transition experience, which is hopefully seamless?
Engineer Note: Hey folks, I'm on the dev team fixing this bug. We're really sorry that this has happened, and we are currently rolling out a fix. Please expect that to land for your site in the next few days. Thanks, Eric

title: Jira Labs feature "New work transition experience" was removed from personal settings and no replacement provided
description: h3. Issue Summary Jira used to allow for Jira Labs feature "New work transition experience" to be enabled on a per-user level. However, following a recent change to how Jira manages experimental features, the toggle has been removed from Personal Settings, with no replacement at either the user or admin level, locking the use of these features. h3. Steps to Reproduce # In Jira, go to *Settings → General Settings (Personal Jira Settings) → Jira Labs* ( /jira/settings/personal/general{}}}). # Verify that there is "New work transition experience" in Jira Labs, however, there is no toggle available to turn it on or off. # As a Jira admin, go to *Settings → System → Beta features* ( /jira/settings/system/labs{}}}). # Verify that feature "New work transition experience" is not available h3. Expected Results Either the Personal Settings toggle should be available, or a site/org-wide selection should be provided to control whether "New work transition experience" feature is to be enabled or disabled. h3. Actual Results Currently, there is no way to control whether users want features enabled or disabled. h3. Workaround Reach out to Atlassian Support to request that the feature toggles be temporarily re-enabled on your site.
comment:
Engineer Note: @engineer You're right that asking every user to switch individually isn't a realistic answer when most of your site is on the classic experience. The in-product switch helps someone who wants to move themselves, but it isn't a substitute for site-level control, and I should have been clearer about that distinction. Here's where we actually are. Rather than adding an admin toggle, we're changing which experience sites default to, so that people end up on the new one without anyone having to opt them in. We're working through existing sites progressively. In the meantime, Support can move your whole site over in one go if you'd like it now. If you've already raised one and it hasn't landed, send me the ticket reference and I'll chase it.
Engineer Note: The in-product switch has now completed rollout and is available on all sites. How to change your experience •  On the new experience, open the transition window and choose Switch to the classic experience from its menu. •  On the classic experience, you'll be offered the option to move to the new one when the transition window opens. The choice applies to your own account and takes effect straight away.  This restores the per-user control that was lost when the Jira Labs toggle was removed, which is what this issue reported, so we're resolving it here. If you need your whole site moved rather than individual accounts, that's still handled by Support and a single request will cover the site. Please raise a new issue if anything isn't working as described above, and thanks to everyone who reported and followed this one.

title: Rearrange gadgets or change dashboard layout is failing
description: h3. Issue Summary Rearrange gadgets or change dashboard layout is failing if the dashboard contains one or more gadgets belonging to a product or app that is no longer installed on your instance or just any broken Jira gadget. h3. Steps to Reproduce # When a product (e.g., Jira Service Management) or a Marketplace app is removed, any gadgets from that product that were previously added to dashboards become "orphaned". # Try moving a gadget from left to right. The request to  # https://abc.atlassian.net/rest/dashboards/1.0/12345/layout returned with status 400 Bad Request h3. Expected Results The gadget should be moved without any issues and orphaned gadgets should be removed from the DB as well. h3. Actual Results The following error observed in the browser logs. Error changing dashboard layout: Gadgets cannot be removed by changing the layout, they need to be removed explicitly h3. Workaround * *Workaround 1* ** Manually create another dashboard with the same gadgets. * *Workaround 2* * ** Run the [GET Gadget|https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/rest/v3/api-group-dashboards/#api-rest-api-3-dashboard-dashboardid-gadget-get:~:text=GET-,Get%20gadgets,-EXPERIMENTAL] API endpoint, and the response of the request will have the Gadget IDs and names. With the gadget's name, identify whether those gadgets are present on the dashboard. If not, those are the problematic orphaned gadgets. Using the gadget ID from the same response, you can use the remove gadget API: [https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/rest/v3/api-group-dashboards/#api-rest-api-3-dashboard-dashboardid-gadget-gadgetid-delete] to delete those gadgets to resolve the issue.
comment: Engineer Note: We have shipped a fix for this. The root cause was any case where a gadget was not installed and not be displayed, the unexpected difference in gadget count then caused an error when updating. A placeholder will now appear for all such cases where a gadget is unable to be displayed.

title: Edit an Inactive workflow displays message "You are viewing an active workflow" when the workflow is inactive

title: Work items with invalid status prevents admins from changing the workflow
description: h3. Issue Summary When a work item has an invalid status, it can cause unexpected behaviours such as the issue not appearing or being unable to change a project’s workflow. A invalid status can be a NULL status value or a status id that does not exist in the issuestatus table. h3. Steps to Reproduce # The steps to replicate this behaviour has not been identified h3. Expected Results Users should be able to transition the work item to a valid status h3. Actual Results # Work item with invalid status (e.g. deleted status) ## Issue visible with status ## Not visible in the list view # Work item with NULL status ## The work item is visible with NO status, thus no option to change the status ## The work item will not be visible in the list view h3. Workaround # Work item with invalid status (e.g. deleted status) ## Can be fixed in work item view by using status drowdown if there is a global status ## Can be fixed in API if there is a global status ## Can be fixed in Bulk edit/ bulk transition the work item # Work item with NULL status ## Can be fixed in API if there is a global status or if there is any status with Global transition ## Can be fixed in Bulk edit/bulk transition if there is any status with Global transition

title: Filtering Work Items by a string that contains a hyphen on All Work or List replaces it with spaces
description: h3. Issue Summary When using the ‘Filter’ on either the List and All Work tabs in a project, if your search term contains a ‘\-’ (hyphen), the generated JQL replaces the ‘\-’ (hyphens) with ‘ ’ (empty spaces), which fails to return work items containing the exact filtered term. Manually fixing the generated JQL (replacing spaces with hyphens) yields the correct results. *Example:* Searching “ aaa-bbbb-ccc ” does not bring items containing the string “ aaa-bbbb-ccc ”, and the resulting Filter > JQL search shows ‘ project = XYZ AND textfields ~ “aaa bbbb ccc* ” ORDER BY created DESC’ Correcting the searched value to ‘ project = XYZ AND textfields ~ “aaa-bbbb-ccc*” ORDER BY created DESC ’ brings the intended results. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Have a Work Item with the summary set as ' aaa-bbbb-ccc '. # Navigate to the project's List/All Work tab. # Using the filter box, type in ' aaa-bbbb-ccc '. h3. Expected Results The Work Item that has the summary ' aaa-bbbb-ccc ' should be returned. h3. Actual Results The work item is not returned. If you click on Filter, then select JQL, you’ll see that the resulting JQL has replaced the hyphens with spaces. * *Expected Result:* } * *Actual Result:* } h3. Workaround As the problem is related to how the 'Filter' generates the JQL, and not exactly a JQL failure, the available workarounds are: * To use Jira's Global Work Item search. * Use the filter, and manually edit the generated JQL by clicking on Filter, then selecting JQL and replacing all spaces with hyphens.

title: Inconsistent Wiki Markup Rendering in Custom Field Descriptions between Global Custom Field Settings and Field Configurations
description: h3. Issue Summary There is a functional discrepancy in how Wiki Markup is rendered for custom field descriptions depending on the administrative interface used to edit the description. Manual Wiki Markup renders correctly when saved via the Global Custom Fields page but fails to render (appearing as plain text) when saved via the Field Configuration page, even though the latter has a Rich Text Editor (ADF) enabled. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Navigate to Jira Settings > Issues > Custom Fields. # Edit a field's description and manually enter Wiki Markup. Save the changes. # View an issue containing this field; observe that the Wiki Markup renders correctly. # Navigate to Jira Settings > Issues > Field Configurations and locate the same field in the relevant configuration scheme. # Edit the description here (where the Rich Text Editor is present) and enter the same manual Wiki Markup. Save the changes. # View the issue again. h3. Expected Results The Wiki Markup should render as formatted text (for example, a panel) regardless of which administration page was used to save the description. h3. Actual Results The description saved via the Field Configuration page renders as literal plain text on the issue view. The rendering engine fails to interpret the markup when the Rich Text Editor is used on this specific page. h3. Workaround If the description is edited via the Field Configuration page, highlighting the manual Wiki Markup and applying a Rich Text format (such as Bold) forces the engine to correctly interpret and render the Wiki Markup on the issue view.

title: Migrating users from Delegated LDAP Authentication directory to internal directory is not migrating users
description: h3. Summary Migrating users from Delegated LDAP Authentication directory to internal directory is not working. h3. Steps to Reproduce # On a clean instance of JIRA 6.4.8, add a user directory using "Internal with LDAP authentication" # Use "Copy User on Logon" checkbox # Login with some AD users so that there are some users in the Delegated LDAP directory. # Now, logging in as the Internal Directory LDAP user, try to migrate users from "Internal with LDAP authentication" directory to Internal directory. # The message comes up : "0 of 2 users successfully migrated." # None of the users are migrated and there is nothing in the logs h3. Expected Results All users from the delegated directory should get migrated to the Internal directory h3. Actual Results The users do not get migrated There are no errors shown up in the logs. h3. Workaround (i) Before proceeding with the workaround, please make a backup of your database so that it is possible to roll back to the original state in case something goes wrong. # Run this query in the database : update cwd_user set external_id = '' where directory_id = <id of the delegated directory you want to migrate> Note : You can get the directory id by hovering over the User directory on the UI and looking at the url for the link. # After changing this value, please restart JIRA. # Now try to run the migration. This time it should run fine. h3. Alternative way to reproduce the bug (!) Another way to reproduce this bug is to create users in the Jira internal directory, and then migrate them to an "Internal with LDAP authentication" directory. When doing that, all the users migrated to the "Internal with LDAP authentication" directory will be automatically given a value in the external_id column. Because of that, such users can't be migrated back to the Jira internal directory, unless this column is cleared for them.

title: Issue key in panel title shifts to panel body after editing in Visual Mode
description: h3. *Issue Summary* When an issue key (e.g., PROJ-1 ) is used in the _title_ parameter of a _panel_ macro, editing the content in *Visual Mode* causes the issue key to be moved from the title into the body of the panel upon re-editing. The bug affects panels in comments and panels in Dashboard Rich Text gadgets. *Why does the problem happen:* The text editor automatically converts plain text issue keys (e.g., PROJ-1 ) into HTML links. The _panel:title=..._ macro expects a plain string. When the Visual Editor renders the title, it wraps the issue key in a link tag. Upon clicking 'Edit' or 'Save', the editor's 'down-converter' (which turns Visual content back into Wiki Markup) fails to realise the link belongs inside the _title_ parameter. It terminates the macro parameter early and places the 'orphaned' link content into the body of the panel. h3. *Steps to Reproduce* # Create a new comment. # In Visual Mode , add a panel and use an issue key in the title (e.g., PROJ-1 ). # Save the comment. # Edit the comment in Visual Mode , modify the panel body (not the title with the issue key) and save the changes. h3. *Expected Results* The panel has the same layout and title before and after editing the panel's body. The underlying markup should look like: Some text. Edited. h3. *Actual Results* The issue key is moved from the panel title to the panel body. The panel has no title anymore. The underlying markup is broken and looks like: PROJ-1 Some text. Edited. h3. *Workaround* *Workaround 1* - Using a table instead of a panel It looks very similar, preserves automatic conversion of plain text issue keys into HTML links, and works in Visual mode. The table is available under the same '+' menu as the panel. *Workaround 2* - Using a panel without a title It looks very similar, preserves automatic conversion of plain text issue keys into HTML links, and works in Visual mode. It requires removing the panel title text and adding the issue key to the panel body. The issue key and other text can be separated by the 'Horizontal ruler' (a horizontal line), which is available in the same '+' menu as the panel. *Workaround 3* - Using Text mode Instead of editing fields containing panels in Visual mode, switch to Text mode (there are 'Visual' and 'Text' buttons at the bottom of the text editor window). Using the Text mode will prevent the editor's 'down-converter' from being used and the panel will be saved in a proper form. *Workaround 4* - Disabling automatic conversion of plain text issue keys into HTML links The problem is triggered by the automatic conversion of plain text issue keys into HTML links. This automatic conversion can be disabled by disabling the ‘ jiraissuelinkrenderer ' module from the ‘ Renderer Component Factories Plugin ' system plugin. This change will prevent the Jira application from automatically converting issue keys into issue links in text fields. This module can’t be disabled from the UI. It needs to be disabled through the database and all of the Jira nodes will need to be restarted (a rolling restart is sufficient) to apply the change. The whole solution is provided in our '[How to disable Jira Issue Key being converted to Issue Link when used in comments/descriptions|https://support.atlassian.com/jira/kb/how-to-disable-jira-issue-key-being-converted-to-issue-link-when-used-in-comments-descriptions/]’ article. h3. *Versions Tested* The bug was tested and confirmed on the following Jira versions: ||Testing Requirements||Version||Affected Version|| |Customers Reported Version|_11.3.10_|_Yes_| |Most Recent Bug-Fix Release|_11.3.10_|_Yes_| |Previous Major Release|_11.2.1_|_Yes_| |Most Recent LTS|_11.3.10_|_Yes_| |Previous Supported LTS|_10.3.24_|_Yes_|

title: The parent status validator and separation of duties conditions do not support case changes in status names
description: h3. Issue Summary Separation of duties condition compares the status name stored in the workflow rule with the status name recorded in issue history when the transition originally occurred. Parent status validators compare the 'name' of the status stored in the workflow rule with the current name of the issues parent status.  If those two names differ only by case, the condition fails to match and the rule no longer behaves as expected. This can happen, for example, after a DC-to-Cloud migration or after a status rename where the workflow rule stores one casing of the status name but issue history still contains the previous casing. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Create a separation of duties condition on a transition in a workflow that references a status "STATUS A" # Create a work item with that workflow applied and transition it through "STATUS A" # The transition should be available on the work item # Change the case of the status name to "Status A" # The transition will now not be available on the work item h3. Expected Results The condition should pass regardless of the the status name changes. h3. Actual Results The condition does not pass if the status names differ in case. h3. Workaround Transition the work item back through the status referenced by the condition.
comment:
Engineer Note: Hey everyone,  We recently addressed an issue with case-insensitive matching in the previous status condition and validator rules as part of https://jira.atlassian.com/browse/JRACLOUD-98043. However, a number of workflow rules still rely on status names rather than stable status IDs, which means they can also be affected by renames and other naming ambiguities over time. The main rules impacted are: * previous status conditions/validators; * Separation of Duties condition; * and parent/child blocking validators. We are going to be looking at a more permanent fix as part of this issue. The direction there is to move from storing and comparing status names in workflow rules to using status IDs instead. That will make workflows more reliable overall and allow users to rename statuses without breaking existing rules.
Engineer Note: Hey everyone,  Thanks for your patience and apologies for the late update. We moved to matching by status ID a few months ago and have found it to be a better experience for matching on these conditions. This means that status renames will no longer cause the conditions to stop working.

title: Unsaved changes count is incorrect on plans on page load
description: h3. Issue Summary The unsaved changes count may show an incorrect count on the plan timeline when the page has loaded. Upon clicking the `Unsaved changes` button and opening the modal, the change count will update to the correct value. This occurs only when there are scenario changes that match the underlying Jira value, essentially "no change", and when the fields that have been changed are not part of the plan, i.e., not rendered in a column, filter, color by, sort by, etc, h3. Steps to Reproduce # Add the `labels` field to a plan timeline. # Select multiple issues via the checkboxes in the plan timeline on the left hand side. # Click the `Bulk actions` button that appears. # Select `Labels` to bulk update labels. # Change the action from `Add labels` to `Remove labels` # Select a label that does not belong to all of the issues. For example, if the `a11y` label does not exist on 3 of the selected issues, try to remove that label. # Click `Apply`. # Reload the page. # Observe the unsaved changes count has some number greater than 0. # Clicking the unsaved changes button resets the unsaved changes count back to its actual, intended value. h3. Expected Results Unsaved changes count matches the actual changes on the plan timeline. h3. Actual Results Unsaved changes count temporarily displays ALL scenario changes on the plan, even if the scenario value is equivalent to the Jira value.   h3. Workaround Click the unsaved changes button after the page has loaded to display the correct number of scenario changes.

title: Field is required message covers field description
description: h3. Issue Summary When creating an issue in Jira Cloud, if a required field (by Field Configuration Scheme) is left empty, the error message ("\ is required") overwrites the field description. This differs from Jira Data Center, where the error message appears below the field description, allowing users to retain important context and guidance. As a result, users in Jira Cloud lose the field description and may not have the necessary information to fill out the field correctly. h3. Steps to Reproduce # In Field Configuration Scheme, configure a required custom field with a description. # Attempt to create an issue, leaving the required field empty, and click "Create". h3. Expected Results The error message ("\ is required") should appear below the field description. The field description should remain visible, providing users with context and guidance for completing the field (as in Jira Data Center): !image-2025-11-03-15-54-18-639.png|width=258,height=100! h3. Actual Results The error message replaces or overwrites the field description. Users cannot see the field description when the error is displayed, which may cause confusion or loss of context: !image-2025-11-03-15-56-21-213.png|width=268,height=100! h3. Workaround Use a *Field Required Validator* on the *"Create" transition* in the workflow. This allows you to specify a custom error message that can include additional context or guidance for the user if the field is not populated.

title: Fix Version field - clicking into field and clicking away fires SET: [] mutation, silently clearing all existing values
description: h3. Issue Summary The Multi-Version Picker inline edit component ( JiraMultipleVersionPickerField{}}}) fires a } with } when a user clicks into the Fix Version field and clicks away without making any selection. This silently removes all existing Fix Versions from the issue. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Open any issue with 2+ Fix Versions assigned # Click into the Fix Version field (dropdown opens) # Click away without selecting or deselecting anything *Mutation fired on blur:* ] } } } *Response confirms data loss:* } } } } } *Reproduction details:* * Reproduced by Atlassian Support on customer instance * Cross-browser: Chrome 151, Chrome Incognito, Edge InPrivate * Several Projects affected * Frontend version: } *Impact:* * Silent data loss, users unaware until they check history * Affects ALL projects site-wide (system field) * All users with edit access are affected * No confirmation dialog or undo h3. Expected Results No change, field retains existing values h3. Actual Results All Fix Versions are removed (set to None) h3. title: "Add option" and other field placeholders are missing for custom fields in Jira Cloud.
description: h3. Issue Summary In Jira Cloud, custom fields that previously displayed descriptive placeholders (such as "Add option", "Add date", or "Add text") when no value was selected have reverted to showing "None" or no placeholder at all. This change affects the user experience by removing clear prompts for data entry. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Log in to a Jira Cloud instance. # Navigate to an issue containing custom fields (e.g., Single Select, Date Time, or Multi-line text). # Ensure the custom field has no value selected/entered. # Observe the placeholder text displayed in the field. h3. Expected Results Fields should display the Content Design approved placeholder values instead of "None": * Single Select / Cascading Select : "Add option" * Multi Select : "Add options" * Date Time : "Add date" * Single/Multi Line Text : "Add text" * Group Picker : "Add group" / "Add groups" h3. Actual Results The fields display "None" or are empty, lacking the descriptive "Add..." prompts that were previously available. h3. Workaround Currently there is no known workaround for this behavior. A workaround will be added here when available
comment: Engineer Note: Hi everyone, This is Rituraj from the Jira Issue View team. This bug is fixed and I confirmed the functionality to be working as expected.  Sincerely, Rituraj Seal

title: Jira Plans: Show incorrect unsave change account and doritos for the incorrect scenarios change
description: h3. Issue Summary "Unsaved changes" counter shows pending changes but the Save Changes dialog displays no work items. The plan reports a non-zero change count and a dot indicator on the affected field, yet when the user clicks to review/save, the scenario change rows are missing. This appears as work items "disappearing" from the save dialog. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Open a Jira Plan that has a custom field (e.g. Customer User Picker) configured. # In the plan timeline, change the custom field value on a work item (e.g. from "ABC" to "XYZ") - the unsaved changes counter increments to 1 # In a separate session (or directly on the Jira issue), update the same field on the underlying issue to the same value selected in step 2 (e.g. also set to "XYZ") # Return to the plan - observe the change counter still shows 1 and a dot indicator appears on the field # Click "Save Changes" / open the Save Changes dialog h3. Expected Results * The plan detects that the scenario value now matches the Jira baseline, automatically clears the scenario change indicator on the field value, and resets the counter to 0 h3. Actual Results * The change counter shows 1 unsaved change and a dot indicator is present on the field * The Save Changes dialog opens empty with no scenario change rows displayed which is correct. * The UI state is inconsistent: the counter says there are changes but nothing is shown to save or discard h3. Workaround Toggle the affected field to any other value, then set it back to the intended value. This forces the frontend to re-evaluate the comparison, the dot indicator disappears, and the change counter resets to 0 as expected.
comment: Engineer Note: This should be resolved now. Thanks for your patience as we fixed the problem. Please do let us know if you continue to experience any inconsistencies in the change count.  Thanks! Josh Jira Plans Software Engineer

title: Switching saved views on plan timeline does not update issues correctly
description: h3. Issue Summary If a user switches to another saved view that relies on fields in the filter and/or sorting preferences of such view, the issues on the plan timeline may be displayed incorrectly.  h3. Steps to Reproduce # Navigate to a Jira plan. # On any saved view (A) , remove all field columns, filters, and color by preferences. # Save the changes for that view. # On another saved view *(B),* add a filter for the `labels` field, any filter value will suffice. Ensure there is at least one issue that matches the filter. # Save that view. # Navigate back to the view *A* and reload the page. # Switch to the other *B* view. # Observe there are no issues visible on the plan timeline. h3. Expected Results Issues should align with the saved view after switching views.  h3. Actual Results Issues are incorrectly displayed as there is not sufficient information loaded to the plan upon switching views. h3. Workaround Reload the page.

title: Updating fields values from a selected issue on Backlog view causes Story Points value to glitch
description: h3. Issue Summary Whenever users are updating any fields of a selected work item from the *Backlog* tab, a glitch occurs on the *Story Points* value from that work item, and users can only see the correct value again after a refresh. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Go to the Backlog of any board that uses Story Points as an estimate method. # Verify that the story points value are displayed as expected in the *Story Points* column. # Select any work item from the list, and update any fields on it. # Observe that the value of Story Points for the same work item glitches on the page, being replaced by an "-" character, and a refresh of the page is required for it to display the expected value once again. h3. Expected Results The *Story Points* field value should continue to display its value. h3. Actual Results The *Story Points* field value starts to display the "-" character instead of the expected value. h3. Workaround The only known workaround at this point is refreshing the page.
comment: Engineer Note: This issue is particularly irritating for users during planning sessions, where a smooth and reliable workflow is essential. The current behaviour disrupts the session flow, creates unnecessary confusion, and costs valuable time for everyone involved. Resolving it would noticeably improve the planning experience.

title: Rovo actions and skills for Jira Plans fail to execute when requiring user confirmation
description: h3. Issue Summary Users attempting to execute Atlassian Rovo skills or actions that interact with Jira Plans (such as creating work items) receive an error during the confirmation step and the action fails to complete. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Open Rovo chat or prompt interface within Jira. # Ask Rovo to perform an action or run a skill on a Jira Plan (e.g., "Create work items in my Jira Plan"). # Attempt to confirm the proposed action in the confirmation prompt. h3. Expected Results The action processes successfully, and the requested items or updates are created in the specified Jira Plan. h3. Actual Results The action fails to complete, and an error is displayed indicating that the action request could not be processed.  h3. Workaround There is currently no direct workaround within Rovo for confirmation-based Jira Plans actions. Users can temporarily create or manage work items manually directly within the Jira Plans interface.
comment: Engineer Note: Thank you for your patience while we investigated this issue. We have identified the underlying cause affecting Jira Plans Rovo skills requiring confirmation (such as creating plan work items or running plan actions resulting in error messages) and have deployed a fix to production. All confirmation actions should now complete successfully without displaying errors. If you are still experiencing any issues with confirmation prompts or actions in Jira Plans, please refresh your session. If the problem persists, feel free to reach out to our team by commenting on this ticket.

title: New workflow editor fails to save changes if transition descriptions contain hidden or invalid characters (e.g., newlines/tabs).
description: h3. Issue Summary When attempting to update a workflow in the new workflow editor, the operation fails with a generic error: "We couldn't save your changes – validation failed". Investigation reveals that the underlying API returns a 400 Bad Request because transition descriptions contain characters that the new editor's validation logic considers invalid (such as tabs or newlines). - These characters are often present in the workflow descriptor's metadata but are not visible in the Jira UI. This issue frequently affects workflows that have existed for a long time or were previously modified via certain APIs/experiences that allowed these characters, which the new editor now strictly validates against. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Navigate to a workflow that contains hidden characters (like \t or \n) in a transition description. # Attempt to make any change (e.g., add a validator or condition). # Click Update Workflow. h3. Expected Results The workflow should save successfully, or the editor should automatically strip/handle the unsupported characters. h3. Actual Results The UI displays: "We couldn't save your changes – validation failed". The network response shows: - ] } h3. Workaround Use the Jira Cloud REST API to identify and update the affected transition descriptions by removing invalid characters. - Reference: [REST API : Bulk update workflows|https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/rest/v3/api-group-workflows/#api-rest-api-3-workflows-update-post]
comment: Engineer Note: Hey everyone, Thanks for your patience. I'm expecting to finish rollout of the change to allow tabs in these descriptions within the next day.
