This does not affect all work items. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Step 1 : Open the child issue where you need to update parent. # Step 2 : Attempt to update the Parent field of that issue from the parent field or the add parent option before the child issue #  Step 3 : Save the Changes h3. Expected Results The parent field should be updated succesfully h3. Actual Results The below exception is thrown in the xxxxxxx.log file: ..."We couldn't update the Parent value. We couldn't save your changes. Copy your content, then try reloading the page." This happens when the in the child issue there was a link that has had been deleted and this caused issue in the backend -This only affects work items where a previously linked issue was deleted, leaving a stale reference behind. - All other work items can have their Parent field updated without issue. h3. Workaround No workaround yet

title: Issue View: Non-descriptive labels for buttons
description: h3. Issue Summary The non-descriptive label "More information about this user" is specified for the buttons. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Open the Jira Cloud homepage. # Navigate to the Sidebar, expand "Spaces", and open any space. # Navigate to the "List" link, activate it, and open any work item from the data table. # Navigate onto the comments section. # Using a screen reader, navigate with down arrow (JAWS/NVDA) or Control+Option+Right/Left arrow (VoiceOver). # Navigate to the mentioned button. # Observe that the button is announced as "More information about this user" instead of a user-specific label, such as "More information about Chirag Goyal". h3. Screenshot !Screenshot 2026-08-19 at 6.12.42 PM.png|width=244,height=130! h3. Actual Results When screen reader users navigate to tagged user buttons in a comment, each button is announced with the same non-descriptive accessible name, such as “More information about this user”. This occurs because the button’s accessible name uses a generic value instead of a user-specific label, such as “More information about Chirag Goyal”. As a result, screen reader users may be unable to determine which person is tagged in the comment or whose information will be displayed when the button is activated. h3. Expected Results The screen reader should announce unique and descriptive labels for the buttons. *Provide a unique and descriptive label, such as “More information about Chirag Goyal” for the button by updating its } attribute.* Note: This code example is intended only as a general illustration of how to address the violation and should not be considered a complete or production-ready solution. If you have any questions, please attach this ticket to a #help-accessibility request. Code Snippet: <button aria-expanded="false" aria-haspopup="true" aria-label="More information about Chirag Goyal" ....> (....) </button> h3. Workaround Currently there is no known workaround for this behavior. A workaround will be added here when available h3. Environment MacBook Pro (16-inch, 2021) macOS Tahoe 26.5.2 Windows 11 Chrome - 151.0.7922.170 (Official Build) (64-bit) Safari- Version 26.5.2 JAWS- Version 2026 NVDA- Version 2026.1 VoiceOver - Version Latest
comment: Engineer Note: Released the fix

title: Create Issue: Insufficient color contrast for the standard text
description: h3. Issue Summary The texts "Summary" and "Add a description or type / for actions and Rovo" fails to meet minimum color contrast requirements. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Open the Jira cloud homepage in dark mode. # Navigate to and activate "Create" button. # Navigate onto the mentioned texts in the "Create New Work Item" dialog. # Use a color contrast testing tool to check the color contrast. # Observe that the color contrast between the mentioned texts and the background is insufficient. h3. Screenshot 1 !image-2026-08-11-17-19-29-034.png|width=195,height=101! h3. Screenshot 2 !image-2026-08-11-17-15-56-858.png|width=195,height=101! h3. Actual Results There are some standard text with background/foreground color combinations having an insufficient contrast ratio. The placeholder texts "Summary" with #7F8088 foreground color and "Add a description or type / for actions and Rovo" with #7E8188 foreground color have an insufficient color contrast ratio of 3.6:1 with #2B2C2F background color. This will make it difficult for people with low vision and color blindness to read standard text elements that have insufficient contrast. h3. Expected Results The contrast ratio between foreground text and background for the standard text should be sufficient. On all pages, ensure that each foreground/background color combination presents a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 for standard text. In this case, ensure that the color contrast of the placeholder texts such as "Summary" and "Add a description or type / for actions and Rovo" meet the minimum contrast ratio of 4.5:1 with it’s background. h3. Workaround Currently there is no known workaround for this behavior. A workaround will be added here when available. h3. Environment MacBook Pro (16-inch, 2021) macOS - Tahoe 26.5.1 Windows - 11 Chrome - Version 151.0.7922.108 (Official Build) (arm64) Safari - Version 26.2 (21623.1.14.11.9)

title: Work item orphaned when switching security schemes
description: h3. Issue Summary A Jira work item can end up with an issue security level assigned that belongs to a different issue security scheme than the one currently associated with the work item's project. The security level still exists, so it is not deleted or orphaned, but it is not valid for the project's active security scheme. This mismatched state surfaces as a generic "Unknown security level" error and prevents access to the affected work item. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Open the affected work item. # Attempt to view or edit the work item, or change its security level, as an administrator. h3. Expected Results An authorized administrator can view the work item and change or clear its issue security level to a value valid for the project's current scheme. h3. Actual Results * The work item cannot be opened normally through the UI. * The page shell loads, but the issue-data APIs deny access (the issue resolves as null and the issue history endpoint returns a permission-masked 404). * The security level cannot be changed through the UI because the assigned value is not part of the project's current scheme. h3. Workaround No supported UI workaround. Adding an administrator directly to the mismatched security level does not restore access. A backend data correction is required to clear the invalid security level on the affected work item.

title: Error 'We couldn’t create the space' while creating the Space using the Space Template
description: h3. Issue Summary Error 'We couldn’t create the space' while creating the Space using the Space Template. The Space is not created and we get an error.  One of the underlying cause for this error is related to the Workflow having the Third-Party App Conditions or Actions added to the transitions.   h3. Steps to Reproduce # In the Workflow transition, add a condition for the Third-party app like Checklist # Save the Workflow and the Space as Template # Try to create a new Space using the above Template and error will be encountered h3. Expected Results The Space should be created and the error should show the clear message h3. Actual Results The Space is not created and we get the error h3. Workaround Edit the Template and uncheck the option for copying Workflow settings. Once the new space is created, manually associate the required Workflow Scheme.

title: When clicking on the child work item/subtask, the redirection starts and returns to the parent instead of loading the child work item/subtask
description: h3. Issue Summary When clicking on the child work item/subtask, the redirection starts and returns to the previous work item/parent instead of loading the child work item/subtask. This affects Epic - Child work item relationships and also Story-subtasks. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Open an Epic in a new tab # Select a child work item or # Open Story work item in a new tab # Select a subtask Note: The issue can be replicated on select instances. h3. Expected Results When clicking on the child work item/subtask, the selected work item should be opened h3. Actual Results When clicking on a child work item, the redirection starts and returns back to the original work item instead of opening the child work item. The redirection works on the second attempt to open the same work item. Note: We see the same behaviour when navigating back to parent through the breadcrumb. h3. title: Viewing an issue link from the Jira Mobile app that contains the "issue" path in the URL will redirect outside the app to the mobile's web browser.
description: h3. Issue Summary Viewing an issue link from the Jira Mobile app that contains the "issue" path in the URL will redirect outside the app to the mobile's web browser. This behavior changes if the issue link contains the "browse" path where the redirection will occur inside the Mobile app. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Add a link to an issue in the Description or comment and make sure the link forwards to the "issue" path. For example https://<instanceName>.atlassian.net/issues/SDP-324 # Open the Jira mobile app and click on the link h3. Expected Results The Mobile app redirects to the issue inside the app. h3. Actual Results The mobile app redirects outside the app h3. Workaround Edit the link to forward to the "browse" path. For example: https://<instanceName>.atlassian.net/browse/SDP-324. This ensures the Mobile app redirects to the issue inside the app.
comment: Engineer Note: Issue is fixed and available in latest version

title: Restrictions to plan viewer permissions behave differently for Calendar, Timeline and Plan's settings.
description: h3. Issue Summary If a plan has restricted viewer and editor permissions, and a user/group is included as an editor of a plan, but not included as a viewer - the user/group is able to see work items on the Timeline, but they are not able to see work items on the Calendar. It may also cause options on Plan's settings not to load for a user not included as a viewer. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Navigate to a plan's settings # Restrict permissions for both editor and viewer # Include user X in editor permissions # Do not include user X in viewer permissions h3. Expected Results User X should be able to view work items in the Timeline and in the Calendar User X should able to see options on Plan's settings section. h3. Actual Results User X can see work items in the Timeline, but cannot see work items in the Calendar User X is not able to see options on Plan's settings section. h3. Workaround Include the user/group explicitly in the viewer permissions
comment: Engineer Note: The bug fix has now been completed. Please reopen ticket if the problem persists.

title: Plans API returns filtered results for admin users instead of all plans
description: h3. Issue Summary The * }* [API endpoint|https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/rest/v3/api-group-plans/#api-rest-api-3-plans-plan-get] does not respect Jira Administrator permissions. An admin user who can view all plans via the UI receives a filtered response through the API, showing only plans directly accessible to them rather than all plans on the instance. This contradicts the documented permission behavior where admin users should be able to see all plans. h3. Steps to Reproduce * Log in as a user with Jira Administrator permissions. * Navigate to Advanced Roadmaps in the UI and note the total number of plans visible (e.g., all plans on the instance). * Make a } request to } using Basic Auth (email + API token) with the same admin account. * Compare the number of plans returned by the API against the total visible in the UI. * Optionally, restrict permissions on a specific plan and confirm it no longer appears in the API response despite the user being an admin. h3. Expected Results The API should return all plans on the instance for a user with Jira Administrator permissions, consistent with the UI behavior and the documented permission model at [Types of permissions in your plan|https://support.atlassian.com/jira-software-cloud/docs/set-permissions-in-advanced-roadmaps/] h3. Actual Results The API returns only plans that are directly accessible to the authenticated user, ignoring their Jira Administrator role. The total count returned by the API does not match the total number of plans on the instance or the number visible in the UI. Plans with restricted permissions are excluded from the API response even for admin users. h3. Workaround Administrators can view the complete list of plans through the Advanced Roadmaps UI. If plan IDs are required programmatically (e.g., for export or automation purposes), customers can contact Atlassian Support to request a data export containing the full list of plan IDs.
comment: Engineer Note: The bug fix has now been completed. Please reopen ticket if the problem persists.

title: Rovo Agent cannot read Jira issue (called via "Start Work" on issue screen) due to IP allowlist

Issue Summary When a Rovo agent is triggered on a work item by clicking "Start work" , the agent cannot read the issue due to IP allowlist blocking, even though IPs are allowlisted for Rovo. Some customers were reporting that the same agent can access the same issue when used via Rovo Chat, but this may not always be true. *Error message seen by the customer:*   } h3. title: When clone feature is disabled in Jira Cloud web, it is still available on Jira Cloud mobile
description: h3. Issue Summary It's possible to disable the Clone feature in Jira Cloud web by adding the below property as true on the status in a workflow. jira.permission.createclone.denied = true However, it's not disabled in Jira Cloud Mobile app.  h3. title: After switching to OpenSearch on Jira, the JQL query "Team is/is not EMPTY" gives "An unknown error occurred while trying to perform a search"
description: h3. Issue Summary After switching to OpenSearch on Jira, the JQL query "Team is/ is not{}}} EMPTY" gives "An unknown error occurred while trying to perform a search". (i) Team is the custom field coming from Advanced Roadmap for Jira. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Switch to OpenSearch 2.19.4 on Jira 11.3.4 # Run the JQL query "Team is/is not EMPTY" # JQL hits this cluster-level limit( *1024 boolean clauses* per query): 2026-05-20 16:53:09,402+0200 http-nio2-8080-exec-18 ERROR xxxx00 1013x379971x1 jpi93p 10.249.14.103 /rest/issueNav/1/issueTable [c.a.j.p.i.service.issuetable.DefaultIssueTableService] Error searching com.atlassian.jira.search.opensearch.exception.OpenSearchSearchException: Failure searching from OpenSearch org.opensearch.client.opensearch._types.ErrorResponse: }}],"grouped":true,"caused_by": ,"reason":"all shards failed","root_cause":[ ],"type":"search_phase_execution_exception"},"status":400} h3. Expected Results Search should complete without an error. h3. Actual Results It gives "An unknown error occurred while trying to perform a search". h3. Workaround If feasible, you may increase the indices.query.bool.max_clause_count setting on your OpenSearch cluster. This is a cluster-level setting applied directly to OpenSearch (not to Jira). Step 1 — Find your OpenSearch connection details Check your jira-config.properties file for: opensearch.http.url=https://your-opensearch-host:9200 opensearch.username=your_username opensearch.password=your_password Step 2 — Apply the new setting From any machine with network access to the OpenSearch cluster (e.g., one of your Jira nodes), run: curl -X PUT "https://<OPENSEARCH_HOST>:<PORT>/_cluster/settings" \ -u <username>:<password> \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d ' }' Replace <OPENSEARCH_HOST>:<PORT>, <username>, and <password> with the values from your jira-config.properties. Note: If you are using AWS OpenSearch Service (managed), you cannot use the REST API for this. Instead, go to AWS Console → OpenSearch Service → Your Domain → Edit → Advanced cluster settings and add indices.query.bool.max_clause_count: 2048. Step 3 — Verify curl -X GET "https://<OPENSEARCH_HOST>:<PORT>/_cluster/settings" \ -u <username>:<password> \ -H "Accept: application/json" You should see "indices.query.bool.max_clause_count": "2048" in the persistent section. Step 4 — Test Re-run your Team is EMPTY JQL query in Jira. It should now return results without errors. No Jira restart or reindex is required.

title: "Recently Created Chart" gadget fails to update its display when a user edits the gadget to select a new filter
description: h3. Issue Summary After upgrading to Jira Data Center 11.3.x, the "Recently Created Chart" gadget fails to update its display when a user edits the gadget to select a new filter. While the edit dialog shows the correct selection, the chart continues to render old data or remains empty. Technical analysis shows that the gadget save action correctly updates the } and } fields, but fails to populate the } field, which the renderer relies on. h3. Steps to Reproduce # Upgrade Jira Data Center to version 11.3.7. # Add a "Recently Created Chart" gadget to a dashboard. # Edit the gadget and select a saved filter (e.g., Filter A). Save the gadget. # Edit the gadget again and change the selection to a different filter (e.g., Filter B). # Observe the gadget display. h3. Expected Results The gadget should refresh and display the chart based on the data from Filter B.   h3. Actual Results The gadget continues to display data from Filter A (or no data if it was a new gadget). A full page refresh is required to see the change, but the underlying preference mapping remains inconsistent. A review of the gadget preferences via } reveals a disconnect: * The } field correctly reflects the new filter ID (e.g., 91801{}}}). * The } field correctly reflects filter{}}}. * *The* } field remains empty ( ""{}}}). Because the Jira 11 gadget renderer specifically looks for the } value to fetch chart data, the chart fails to update because this field is never written during the save operation. *JSON Evidence (from* } endpoint):   , , }}   h3. Workaround Standard UI workarounds (full page refresh, clearing browser cache) have been reported as *ineffective* by the customer but working locally. The gadget remains in a broken state because the } preference is never successfully written to the database during the save operation.   *Note:* This is affecting Jira 11.3.7 but I was not able to select it during this ticket creation

Example: Quick Search input: 横浜 -> JQL: text ~ "よこはま" Quick Search input: 横浜で -> JQL: text ~ "横浜で" Quick Search input: a横浜 -> JQL: text ~ "a横浜" The symptom occurred on Jira/JSM 11.x, but not 10.x and before. h3.
